messages.author: dana-okafor

It looks like it started around 6:40 AM their time and drivers are already backing up at the guard shack because the tablets are just spinning.

messages.author: ilse-varga

messages.author: samir-patel

messages.author: dana-okafor

messages.author: samir-patel

messages.author: dana-okafor

# Order Form: Brackenwater Freight Co. (2024-2025 term)

## 1. Parties and Record

This Order Form is between Pemberline Systems and Brackenwater Freight Co. for the subscription specified below. The subscribed product is Pemberline Dock, Pemberline Systems’ yard and dock scheduling software.

This instrument was drafted on 2024-11-01. The executed record was prepared on 2024-11-12 by June Osei-Lark, Deal desk and contracts manager, for inclusion in the order file. Brackenwater Freight Co. is identified in the associated setup materials by the abbreviations BWF and Bracken; those abbreviations refer to the same customer named in this instrument.

## 2. Execution and Effective Date

Both parties signed this Order Form on 2024-11-12. The effective date is 2024-12-01.

The execution date records the parties’ signatures. The effective date identifies the commencement of the subscription described herein. These dates are distinct; execution on 2024-11-12 does not replace or advance the stated effective date.

The signature block below forms part of this executed record.

## 3. Subscription and Commercial Schedule

The subscription is recorded as follows:

| Item | Order specification |
|---|---|
| Customer | Brackenwater Freight Co. |
| Supplier | Pemberline Systems |
| Product | Pemberline Dock |
| Subscribed seats | 60 |
| Price per seat per year | USD 1,700 |
| Discount | 8% |
| Effective date | 2024-12-01 |
| End of current term / renewal date | 2025-11-30 |

The annual per-seat price and the discount are stated separately. The discount applicable to this order is eight percent. The subscribed quantity is sixty seats.

The end of the current term, recorded as the renewal date, is 2025-11-30. That date is separate from both the drafting date and the execution date.

## 4. Operational Identification

Brackenwater Freight Co. operates in less-than-truckload freight in the Great Lakes region. The implementation worksheet accompanying the order file identifies the receiving desk, outbound dispatch desk, and evening yard desk as the initial points for collection of user details.

The worksheet includes a sample scheduling sequence for Door 14: an inbound trailer arrival, a receiving appointment, and an outbound door reassignment. It also includes a second-shift example in which dispatch moves a delayed pickup from the active door list to the next available appointment slot.

These entries describe the operational examples collected for setup review. They do not alter the subscribed seat quantity, annual per-seat price, discount, effective date, or term-end date stated in Section 3.

## 5. Administrative Handling

The order file includes this executed instrument and the setup worksheet titled “BWF Door Schedule — Initial Review.” The worksheet contains a column for shift designation and a separate column for the email address used at sign-in.

The receiving desk is collecting spelling corrections for the user list. Outbound dispatch is reviewing the Door 14 example against its paper appointment board. The evening yard desk is marking entries that represent shared desk labels rather than individual users. These administrative tasks concern setup preparation only.

## 6. Signatures

**For Brackenwater Freight Co.**

Signed: /s/ Lena Morcant  
Name: Lena Morcant  
Date signed: 2024-11-12

**For Pemberline Systems**

Signed: /s/ June Osei-Lark  
Name: June Osei-Lark  
Title: Deal desk and contracts manager

# Brackenwater renewal: customer redline

**Record Type:** Renewal Order Form and Operational Addendum (Customer Markup — For Review Only; Unsigned)  
**Record Date:** 2025-10-28  
**Routing Note:** Received from Brackenwater Freight Co. outside counsel on the morning of October 28, 2025, with redline insertions to Section 3 and Section 5. Logged to the Deal Desk repository for finance sign-off by Anselm Grieve and operational review prior to signature circulation.

---

### 1. Parties and Governing Agreement

**1.1 Identification of Parties.** This Renewal Order Form and Operational Addendum ("Renewal Addendum") is entered into by and between **Pemberline Systems**, a Delaware corporation having its principal place of business at 410 Mercer Wharf, Suite 800 ("Provider"), and **Brackenwater Freight Co.** ("Customer" or "BWF"), a Michigan corporation operating less-than-truckload freight terminals across the Great Lakes region, with administrative offices at 1900 Lakefront Industrial Parkway, Toledo, Ohio. Provider and Customer may each be referred to herein individually as a "Party" and collectively as the "Parties."

**1.2 Reference to Master Agreement.** This Renewal Addendum supplements and modifies that certain Master Subscription Services Agreement between the Parties, together with all prior schedules and attachments thereto (collectively, the "Agreement"), governing Customer's access to and use of the **Pemberline Dock** yard and dock scheduling software platform (the "Hosted Service"). Except as expressly amended by the numbered provisions set forth herein, the terms and conditions of the Agreement shall remain in full force and effect. In the event of an irreconcilable conflict between the body of the Agreement and this Renewal Addendum, the provisions of this Renewal Addendum shall prevail solely with respect to the renewal period governed hereby.

---

### 2. Commercial Renewal Schedule

**2.1 Subscribed Seat Allocation.** Subject to Customer's timely remittance of applicable fees, Provider grants to Customer a non-exclusive, non-transferable right to provision and maintain **75 subscribed seats** for the Hosted Service during the applicable renewal term. Subscribed seats are priced and allocated on a per-seat, per-year basis in accordance with Provider's standard licensing metrics.

**2.2 Named User Reassignment.** Each subscribed seat shall be assigned to an individual, named terminal clerk, yard spotter, dispatcher, or gate attendant employed or contracted by Brackenwater Freight Co. Customer may reassign a seat from a departing or transferred employee to a replacement employee without additional charge during shift rotations, provided that the aggregate number of active concurrent credentials provisioned across all BWF facilities does not exceed seventy-five (75) at any given time.

**2.3 Promotional and Commercial Discount.** In consideration of Customer's multi-terminal deployment and volume commitment hereunder, a commercial discount of **15%** shall be applied to Provider's prevailing per-seat annual list price for the 75 subscribed seats specified in Section 2.1. Pursuant to Provider's internal corporate governance policies, any discount exceeding ten percent (10%) requires the written authorization of Provider's Chief Financial Officer, Anselm Grieve, prior to final execution of this instrument by Provider.

---

### 3. Terminal Operations and Configuration Provisions (Customer Redline Insertions)

**3.1 Cross-Dock Gate Check-In Hardware.** *(Customer Counsel Insertion, 2025-10-28):* Provider acknowledges that Customer's third-shift freight handlers at the Toledo Central Hub (specifically Dock Doors 14 through 38) and the Grand Rapids West satellite yard utilize ruggedized handheld barcode scanners mounted to yard hostler cabs. Provider shall ensure that the Pemberline Dock mobile web view retains backward compatibility with Customer's existing Zebra TC77 handheld fleet without requiring firmware upgrades during peak mid-week LTL consolidation windows (Tuesday 22:00 Eastern through Friday 06:00 Eastern).

**3.2 Automated Detention Log Exports.** *(Customer Counsel Insertion, Oct 28):* Following the carrier dispute incident logged under Support Ticket #PD-88412 on October 14, 2025, regarding trailer dwell timestamps at the Milwaukee South Annex (Gate B), Provider agrees that the daily *Carrier Dwell & Yard Velocity CSV Report* shall automatically generate and deposit into Customer's designated SFTP directory no later than 04:30 Central Time each business day. Such report shall capture tractor arrival scan, gate pass issuance, dock door bump timestamp, and seal verification sign-off for each LTL linehaul trailer.

**3.3 Temporary Yard Overflow Rules.** In the event that winter weather advisories in the Great Lakes corridor require Customer to stage inbound pup trailers along the perimeter gravel lot at the Kalamazoo terminal, Customer's yard supervisors may generate unlimited virtual drop-spots within the Pemberline Dock yard map interface. Virtual drop-spots do not consume additional subscribed seats, provided that no additional user logins are created beyond the 75 seats authorized in Section 2.1.

---

**4.1 Billing Platform.** All invoices generated pursuant to this Renewal Addendum shall be issued through Provider's designated billing vendor, **Stoneharrow Billing**, and transmitted electronically to Customer's Accounts Payable department at `ap-freight@brackenwater.invalid`. Any technical inquiries regarding electronic data interchange (EDI 210/810) formatting or remittance portal credentials may be directed through Provider's deal desk to Felix Duarte at Stoneharrow Billing.

**4.2 Execution Mechanics.** This Renewal Addendum shall not bind either Party unless and until executed by authorized signatories of both Parties below. # Pellow Home Living renewal order form v2

**DRAFT — NOT SIGNED**

**Drafted: March 9, 2026**

## 1. Parties and Subject Matter

This draft renewal order form identifies **Pemberline Systems** as the supplier and **Pellow Home Living** as the customer. The subject matter is the renewal of the customer’s subscription to **Pemberline Dock**, Pemberline Systems’ yard and dock scheduling software.

This document is version 2 of the proposed renewal order form. It is a draft only and has never been signed. The signature spaces below remain blank. Its preparation date is not an execution date or the commencement date of a renewal term.

## 2. Customer Identification

Pellow Home Living is a home goods retailer operating in the Mid-Atlantic. The customer was renamed from **Covey & Lark Retail** on **February 16, 2026**. References to Covey & Lark Retail in historical receiving records concern the former customer name.

For purposes of this draft, the customer name is Pellow Home Living. The former name is included solely to assist personnel reviewing receiving schedules, appointment exports, and other materials generated before the name change. It is not the name presented for customer execution.

## 3. Subscription Quantity

The subscribed seat quantity set by this draft renewal order form is **50 seats**.

The quantity is expressed as a total subscription quantity, not as a count of dock doors, distribution sites, carrier companies, appointment slots, or daily vehicle movements. For example, a receiving schedule containing appointments at Doors 3, 4, and 5 does not establish three additional seats. Likewise, the presence of a carrier name in an appointment record does not itself identify that carrier as a subscribed user.

## 4. Product and Pricing Basis

The product identified in this draft is Pemberline Dock. Pemberline Systems prices Pemberline Dock per seat per year.

The annual, per-seat pricing basis describes the product’s commercial model; it does not convert the preparation date of this draft into a subscription anniversary. Operational references below describe anticipated scheduling activity and do not establish a separate product purchase. In particular, discussion of receiving lanes, furniture unloading, and appointment reports concerns the use of Pemberline Dock rather than an additional software offering.

## 5. Receiving Operations Context

The renewal review concerns the use of Pemberline Dock by receiving personnel coordinating inbound home goods deliveries. The working operations example is a morning receiving board showing upholstered furniture at Door 4, flat-packed shelving at Door 5, and a mixed housewares trailer awaiting a door assignment.

The receiving desk uses the board to distinguish a booked arrival from a vehicle physically present in the yard. Those statuses are operationally different: a carrier’s appointment may remain on the schedule even when the driver has not yet checked in.

## 6. Appointment Review

The customer’s receiving supervisor has requested that the morning appointment view remain readable during the shift handover. The example under review involves two furniture trailers booked close together, with one driver reporting an earlier arrival than the dispatch estimate.

The practical review will examine the appointment time, check-in entry, assigned door, and receiving notes as separate items. The purpose is to avoid treating a changed arrival estimate as evidence that unloading has begun. The proposed subscription quantity remains 50 seats irrespective of the number of appointments displayed during that review.

## 7. Named-User Working List

The operational working list includes receiving desk staff, shift supervisors, and personnel who reconcile the prior day’s arrivals against the appointment board. The customer’s scheduling coordinator is assembling that list from the current shift roster.

The coordinator will distinguish personnel who actively use Pemberline Dock from employees merely mentioned in unloading instructions. A note stating “ask the floor lead before opening Door 5” is an instruction within a receiving record; it is not, by itself, a request to add the floor lead to the working list of users.

## 8. Reporting Review

The report selected for the operational walkthrough is the **Morning Arrival Exceptions** export. The walkthrough will use a receiving day containing an early arrival, a late arrival, and a trailer whose door assignment changed after check-in.

The receiving analyst will compare the exported rows with the corresponding appointment entries. Particular attention will be given to the customer name appearing in the report heading and to notes retained from the period before the name change. Historical text containing Covey & Lark Retail may explain an older entry without changing the customer identified in Section 1.

## 9. Operational Follow-Up

The receiving desk will provide a sample appointment showing the difference between a planned arrival and an actual check-in. The shift supervisor will provide the handover view used before the first furniture delivery is unloaded.

The scheduling coordinator will review the user working list alongside those examples. These activities concern the practical preparation for the renewal discussion. They do not constitute customer signature, supplier signature, or execution of this draft. No completed operational walkthrough shall be represented as acceptance of the order form.

## 10. Version and Draft Status

This document bears the designation “v2” to distinguish it from the earlier working version of the renewal order form. Its subscribed seat quantity is 50.

The draft designation applies to the entire document, including the subscription quantity and signature block. Neither a printed copy placed at the receiving desk nor a copy circulated with the Morning Arrival Exceptions export constitutes a signed order. This draft remains unsigned; both execution lines are intentionally blank.

This Order Form was drafted on 11/25/24. The execution record set forth below was completed on 12/9/24. June Osei-Lark, Deal Desk and Contracts Manager for Pemberline, prepared this executed record on 12/9/24.

## 2. Execution Date and Effective Date

The parties signed this Order Form on **12/9/24**. The subscription effective date is **1/1/25**.

The execution date and effective date are separate dates. Execution on 12/9/24 records the parties’ acceptance of this Order Form; it does not change the subscription effective date to 12/9/24.

For order-entry purposes, the signature date shall be recorded in the execution field and 1/1/25 shall be recorded in the subscription effective-date field. The subscription shall not be entered as commencing in December merely because the parties completed signatures during that month.

## 3. Subscription Ordered

Customer subscribes to **55 seats** of Pemberline Dock. The subscription is priced per seat per year in United States dollars.

| Order field | Agreed value |
|---|---:|
| Product | Pemberline Dock |
| Subscribed seats | 55 |
| Price per seat per year, USD | $1,820.00 |
| Discount | 6% |
| Effective date | 1/1/25 |
| End of current term / renewal date | 12/31/25 |

The seat quantity entered in the subscription record shall be 55. Operational descriptions, shift rosters, and user-assignment worksheets accompanying the order are administrative materials and do not replace the quantity stated in this section.

## 4. Price Calculation

The annual subscription calculation for the stated seat quantity is as follows:

| Calculation | Amount, USD |
|---|---:|
| 55 seats × $1,820.00 per seat per year | $100,100.00 |
| Less 6% discount | ($6,006.00) |
| Net annual subscription amount | **$94,094.00** |

The discount is applied to the aggregate annual seat price shown above. The resulting discounted annual price per seat is $1,710.80.

The pricing worksheet and order-entry summary shall use the same seat quantity, annual unit price, and discount percentage. In particular, the undiscounted annual amount shall remain visible as the calculation base rather than being replaced with the net amount in the unit-price field.

## 5. Current Term and Renewal Record

The current subscription term commences on **1/1/25** and ends on **12/31/25**. The end-of-current-term date, identified in the order record as the renewal date, is **12/31/25**.

The date 12/31/25 shall be entered consistently in the order summary and renewal calendar. The renewal calendar entry should identify the product as Pemberline Dock and the customer as Driftmoor Marine Freight so that it can be distinguished from Customer’s ordinary berth, vessel, and dispatch calendar entries.

This Order Form records the dates and commercial amounts stated herein. It does not set out a separate schedule of renewal pricing.

The operational handoff accompanying this order concerns Customer’s Puget Sound freight movements and the coordination of yard arrivals with dock availability. # SUP-3988: barge slot notifications not sent

| Field | Details |
|---|---|
| Opened | 8/26/25 |
| Customer | Driftmoor Marine Freight |
| Customer code | DMF |
| Product | Pemberline Dock |
| Status | Investigating |
| Area | Barge scheduling / outbound notifications |
| Reported impact | Dispatch did not receive notifications for two changed barge slots |
| Next check | Compare notification events for original bookings and subsequent slot changes |

## Issue

The morning dispatcher reported that two barge slot changes appeared on the scheduling board but did not generate the expected email notifications. Dispatch caught the changes while checking the berth view before the shift handoff; the printed arrival sheet still showed the earlier times.

The affected bookings are at the south landing, berth 2. Both were moved from the morning window into the afternoon. No duplicate bookings or missing slot records were visible during the screen share.

## Update log

**8/26/25, 9:10 AM** — Opened after the dispatcher forwarded screenshots of the board and the shared dispatch inbox. Asked the team to keep the original messages intact and send booking references rather than forwarding another screenshot of the arrival sheet.

**8/26/25, 9:42 AM** — Compared bookings B-1842 and B-1847 with an unchanged booking from the same shift. Recipient addresses match. The dispatcher also checked junk mail and the inbox rules folder; neither notification was there. Thanks to the morning crew for checking between radio calls.

**8/26/25, 10:25 AM** — Reproduced a slot-time edit on a test booking. The board saved the new time, but no corresponding notification appeared in the event view. Initial booking notifications are appearing normally in the same test.

**8/26/25, 11:05 AM** — Sent the reproduction steps and booking references to support engineering. Dispatch will use the board during handoff and call the berth coordinator for today’s changes. Next update after the event trace review.

# Master Subscription Agreement: Marrow Fieldworks and Covered Affiliates

**Drafted:** 24 Mar 2025

## 1. Parties and Purpose

1.1 This Master Subscription Agreement (“Agreement”) is entered into by Pemberline Systems (“Pemberline”) and Marrow Fieldworks, for itself and its covered affiliate, Marrow Agrisupply (together, the “Customer”). Marrow Agrisupply is a subsidiary of Marrow Fieldworks and is expressly included within this Agreement.

1.2 This Agreement records the Customer’s subscription to Pemberline Dock, Pemberline’s yard and dock scheduling software. Marrow Fieldworks operates an agricultural equipment dealer network in the Plains. Marrow Agrisupply operates a farm supply retail chain in the Plains. Each entity’s subscription is separately identified below.

## 2. Execution and Effective Date

2.1 This Agreement was drafted on 24 Mar 2025 and executed by the parties on 8 Apr 2025. The date of execution is distinct from the effective date.

2.2 The Agreement becomes effective on 1 May 2025. Preparatory activities before that date, including roster collection, site naming, and review of sample appointment records, do not alter the effective date or the subscription quantities stated herein.

2.3 The end of the current term, designated as the renewal date, is 30 Apr 2026 for both Marrow Fieldworks and Marrow Agrisupply.

## 3. Subscription Schedule

3.1 The following subscription schedule applies:

| Subscribing entity | Subscribed seats | Price per seat per year (USD) | Discount | End of current term (renewal date) | Support SLA tier |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---|---|
| Marrow Fieldworks | 90 | 1,800 | 10% | 30 Apr 2026 | Tier 2 |
| Marrow Agrisupply | 25 | 1,800 | 10% | 30 Apr 2026 | Tier 2 |

3.2 The stated annual per-seat price and discount apply to each entity listed in the schedule. The seat quantities are entity-specific: 90 seats apply to Marrow Fieldworks, and 25 seats apply to Marrow Agrisupply.

3.3 References to the Customer collectively shall not obscure the separate subscription entries. Administrative rosters, support submissions, and deployment worksheets shall identify the relevant subscribing entity by its full name.

## 4. Covered Affiliate

4.1 Marrow Agrisupply is the covered affiliate under this Agreement. Its inclusion permits its subscription to be administered within this master record while retaining the separate seat quantity shown in Section 3.

4.2 Marrow Fieldworks shall identify whether an operational request concerns Marrow Fieldworks, Marrow Agrisupply, or both. A request to configure a receiving calendar for Marrow Agrisupply shall not be treated as a request to change a Marrow Fieldworks calendar merely because the entities share an administrative contact.

4.3 Site labels shall distinguish the agricultural equipment receiving operation from the farm supply receiving operation. Similar location names shall be accompanied by the subscribing entity’s name in the deployment worksheet.

## 5. Deployment Records

5.1 The Customer shall prepare a deployment worksheet identifying site names, dock-door labels, receiving shifts, and personnel responsible for maintaining appointment calendars. The worksheet shall separate equipment deliveries from farm supply deliveries where those activities use different receiving areas.

5.2 Initial configuration review shall include representative appointment entries for an equipment unloading bay and a retail replenishment dock. Test entries shall be visibly marked as samples and shall not be issued to a carrier as live delivery instructions.

5.3 Where a location uses labels such as “Door 3” or “West Receiving,” the Customer shall use those labels consistently in its worksheet and appointment instructions. Informal directions such as “the usual gate” shall be replaced with the applicable site and receiving-area designation.

## 6. User Administration

6.1 The Customer shall maintain separate user rosters for Marrow Fieldworks and Marrow Agrisupply. Each roster shall identify the user’s business email address, subscribing entity, and operational function, including receiving clerk, dispatcher, or site administrator.

6.2 Shared shift responsibilities shall be described in the roster without substituting a generic shift label for an individual user’s identity. Departure and reassignment notices shall identify the affected user and entity so that administrative changes can be applied to the correct subscription record.

6.3 Before submitting a roster revision, the Customer shall check for duplicate entries caused by shortened names, alternate email addresses, or transfers between equipment and farm supply operations.

## 7. Appointment Information

7.1 The Customer shall supply operational information appropriate to yard and dock scheduling, including appointment reference, carrier name, scheduled arrival, destination site, and receiving location.

7.2 Appointment notes shall distinguish between scheduling instructions and descriptions of goods. For example, an instruction to report to the west gate shall be entered as an arrival instruction rather than embedded in a description of replacement tractor components.

7.3 The Customer shall review imported appointment data for obsolete door names, missing site references, and duplicate delivery references. A corrected import file shall identify the affected records rather than requiring receiving personnel to infer which appointment should remain active.

## 8. Support Administration

8.1 The support SLA tier applicable to both Marrow Fieldworks and Marrow Agrisupply is Tier 2.

8.2 A support submission shall identify the subscribing entity, affected site, relevant appointment reference, observed behavior, and steps preceding the issue. Where available, the submission shall include a screenshot showing the affected calendar or appointment view.

8.3 For a report that an appointment appears under the wrong receiving shift, the Customer shall include the intended shift and the displayed shift. For a report concerning a missing dock-door label, the Customer shall provide the label used in its deployment worksheet. These particulars support investigation and do not change the subscribed support tier.

## 9. Operational Review

9.1 The Customer’s receiving personnel shall review sample calendars before using them for live scheduling. Review shall cover site selection, door naming, shift boundaries, and the clarity of carrier-facing arrival instructions.

9.2 Review comments shall identify a specific screen, field, or appointment example. A comment such as “wrong dock” shall be supplemented with the intended receiving location.

9.3 The parties shall maintain deployment corrections separately from the subscription schedule. Correcting a door label or removing a duplicate sample appointment shall not amend the commercial entries in Section 3.

# Order Form: Orlavine Medical Supply

## 1. Document Identification

**Drafted:** 9/15/25  
**Written and executed:** 9/29/25  
**Effective date:** 10/1/25

This Order Form records the subscription order between Pemberline Systems and Orlavine Medical Supply for Pemberline Dock, a yard and dock scheduling software product. The execution date and the effective date are separate dates. Both parties signed this Order Form on 9/29/25; the subscription described herein becomes effective on 10/1/25.

The administrative account abbreviation for Orlavine Medical Supply is **OMS**. The full customer name, rather than the abbreviation alone, shall appear on the executed order record.

## 2. Parties

**Provider:** Pemberline Systems.

**Customer:** Orlavine Medical Supply, a medical supply distributor operating in the Mountain West.

References to “Provider” and “Customer” in this Order Form mean the entities identified in this section. References to receiving personnel, dispatch personnel, site coordinators, or other operational users describe functions within Customer’s scheduling activities and do not identify additional contracting parties.

The Customer named in this Order Form is Orlavine Medical Supply. Orlavene Health is a separate hospital group and is not a party to this Order Form.

## 3. Subscription Ordered

Customer subscribes to **50 seats** of Pemberline Dock.

The subscribed product is intended for yard and dock scheduling. Customer’s implementation worksheet identifies receiving appointments, outbound staging appointments, and gate-arrival review as the initial operational uses. The worksheet uses separate labels for “Scheduled Arrival” and “Actual Gate Arrival” so that receiving personnel can distinguish an appointment time from a driver’s recorded arrival.

Those worksheet entries provide operational context for setup. They do not change the subscribed product or the number of seats ordered. A dock-door label, appointment category, carrier record, or report heading is not a separate subscription quantity under this Order Form.

## 4. Price and Discount

The price per subscribed seat per year is **USD 1,900**.

The discount applicable to this order is **5%**.

The stated seat quantity, annual per-seat price, and discount are the commercial entries for this subscription. Internal setup worksheets and correspondence concerning receiving shifts shall reproduce those entries without alteration when referring to this order.

Operational references to appointment volume, dock-door usage, or the number of trucks expected during a receiving window do not replace the subscribed-seat quantity. In particular, the receiving worksheet’s count of dock doors is a configuration reference and is not the basis for the subscription price.

## 5. Current Term and Renewal Date

The subscription’s effective date is **10/1/25**.

The end of the current term, recorded as the renewal date, is **9/30/26**.

The signed order record shall retain both dates in their respective fields. The execution date of 9/29/25 shall not be entered in place of the effective date. Likewise, the drafting date of 9/15/25 shall remain a document-preparation date and shall not be used as the start of the subscription.

For the receiving-team handoff, the order reference sheet shall display “Effective: 10/1/25” and “Current term ends / renewal date: 9/30/26.” Calendar entries used for internal preparation shall remain separate from these subscription dates.

## 6. Operational Setup Record

Customer’s receiving supervisor, Tessa Vale, has supplied a preliminary door list for the Mesa Receiving site. The list identifies Door 2 for parcel consolidation, Door 4 for palletized medical supplies, and Door 6 for outbound staging. These descriptions are setup labels, not additions to the commercial terms.

The appointment template shall distinguish the morning receiving shift from afternoon outbound staging. Customer’s dispatch coordinator, Nolan Beck, is preparing the carrier-name worksheet and checking duplicate entries for carriers that appear under both an abbreviated name and a full dispatch-office name.

The proposed “Daily Door Queue” report shall show the appointment reference, carrier name, scheduled arrival, assigned door, and arrival status. A sample appointment, OMS-TEST-014, is marked as a training entry so that receiving personnel do not mistake it for an actual inbound load.

These details are included to make the initial handoff usable by the personnel preparing the scheduling workspace. They do not establish additional seats, prices, discounts, or service commitments.

## 7. Execution and Administrative Handoff

Before the operational handoff, Customer’s setup worksheet shall be checked for legible door names and consistent shift labels. Tessa Vale is to resolve the worksheet entry currently labeled “rear receiving” by identifying the corresponding numbered door. Nolan Beck is to remove the duplicate carrier entry from the sample appointment list.

The executed copy shall be retained with the order record. The receiving-team packet shall contain the door worksheet and sample report layout separately, allowing operational corrections without replacing this signed Order Form.

The signatures below record execution by both parties on 9/29/25. Execution does not alter the effective date of 10/1/25 or the current-term end and renewal date of 9/30/26.

## 1. Parties and Background

**1.1 Identification of Parties.** This Renewal Order Form (the "Renewal Order Form") is entered into by and between Pemberline Systems ("Pemberline") and Orlavine Medical Supply ("Customer," and together with Pemberline, the "Parties"). This document was initially drafted on 9/8/26, is executed by the authorized representatives of both Parties on 9/24/26 (the "Execution Date"), and shall take commercial and legal effect on 10/1/26 (the "Effective Date"). For clarity, the Execution Date of 9/24/26 governs the binding commitment of the Parties hereto, whereas the Effective Date of 10/1/26 marks the commencement of the renewal subscription period described herein.

**1.2 Reference to Governing Agreement.** This Renewal Order Form is governed by and incorporated into the existing master subscription agreement and prior ordering documentation previously entered into between Pemberline and Customer (collectively, the "Prior Agreement"). This Renewal Order Form amends, supersedes, and replaces the applicable commercial terms of the Prior Agreement solely with respect to the renewal period and per-seat pricing set forth below. Except as expressly modified by the terms of this Renewal Order Form, all terms, conditions, exhibits, and operational schedules of the Prior Agreement shall remain in full force and effect. In the event of any conflict or inconsistency between the provisions of the Prior Agreement and the provisions of this Renewal Order Form, the provisions of this Renewal Order Form shall control with respect to the subject matter hereof.

---

## 2. Subscription Scope and Operational Deployment

**2.1 Licensed Software.** Subject to the terms of the Prior Agreement and this Renewal Order Form, Pemberline grants to Customer a continuing right to access and use Pemberline Dock, Pemberline's proprietary yard and dock scheduling software platform (the "Service"). Access to the Service is licensed on a named-seat basis per year. Each individual user credential assigned to Customer personnel—including gate security officers, cold-chain receiving clerks, yard spotter dispatchers, and regional warehouse supervisors—constitutes a single seat assignment under Customer's production instance (`oms-mtn-prod`).

**2.2 Covered Facilities and Operational Environment.** Customer's deployment of the Service under this Renewal Order Form encompasses Customer's medical supply distribution operations across the Mountain West region. Specifically, the production configuration maintained under this Renewal Order Form supports:
*   **Salt Lake North Distribution Center (West Valley City, UT):** Inbound and outbound scheduling for Doors 1 through 28, including the dedicated temperature-controlled biologics receiving bays (Doors 14 through 19) and the sterile surgical kit staging yard (Yard Zone B).
*   **Boise Sterile Annex (Meridian, ID):** Dock scheduling for Doors 1 through 10, cross-dock transfer lanes, and drop-trailer lot tracking for regional courier fleets.
*   **Denver Regional Hub (Aurora, CO):** High-turn parcel and LTL freight doors (Doors 1 through 22), carrier self-scheduling portal access for third-party medical freight carriers, and automated gate kiosk check-in workflows.

**2.3 Technical Configuration Continuity.** The custom configuration parameters established during prior operational periods—specifically the automated detention alert rules associated with the `Cold-Chain-Dwell-Summary-v3` report and the webhook integration linking Pemberline Dock to Customer's warehouse management system (reference Engineering Ticket `PD-44918`, resolved following the August gate-house scanner firmware update at the Salt Lake North facility)—shall carry forward without interruption upon the Effective Date of 10/1/26.

---

## 3. Commercial Terms and Pricing

**3.1 Per-Seat Subscription Rate.** Commencing on the Effective Date of 10/1/26 and continuing through the expiration of the Renewal Term defined in Section 4.1, the subscription fee for Pemberline Dock under this Renewal Order Form shall be **USD $1,960 per seat per year**. This rate supersedes the per-seat rate set forth in the Prior Agreement.

**3.2 Seat Reallocation and Administrative Controls.** Customer's designated system administrators at the Salt Lake North, Boise, and Denver facilities may reassign active seat credentials among bona fide employees and onsite contractors when shift rotations or personnel changes occur (such as seasonal adjustments between the first-shift receiving crew and the third-shift hospital courier loading team), provided that the total number of concurrent active named seats does not exceed Customer's contracted seat allocation, and provided further that single seat credentials are not shared simultaneously across multiple individuals or terminal workstations at the dock doors.

**3.3 Invoicing and Remittance.** Invoices issued pursuant to this Renewal Order Form shall reference Customer Vendor Code `OMS-VEND-8841` and shall be transmitted electronically to Customer's accounts payable department in accordance with the billing procedures established under the Prior Agreement. All monetary amounts stated in this Renewal Order Form are denominated in United States Dollars (USD) and are exclusive of applicable state, local, or municipal sales and use taxes imposed by taxing authorities in Utah, Idaho, or Colorado.

---

## 4. Term and Renewal Schedule

**4.1 Renewal Term.** Notwithstanding the Execution Date of 9/24/26, the renewal term governed by this Renewal Order Form shall commence at 12:00 a.m. Mountain Time on **10/1/26** (the Effective Date) and shall continue in full force and effect until 11:59 p.m. Mountain Time on **9/30/27** (the "Renewal Date" and end of the current term), unless earlier terminated in accordance with the provisions of the Prior Agreement.

**4.2 Transition from Prior Term.** The Parties acknowledge that the subscription period under the Prior Agreement remains active through the close of business on 9/30/26. There shall be no lapse in production service availability, carrier portal access, or historical dock audit log retention during the transition between the expiration of the prior period and the Effective Date of 10/1/26.

---

## 5. General Provisions and Operational Notices

**5.1 Infrastructure and Hosting Environment.** Customer acknowledges that the Pemberline Dock application environment is hosted via Pemberline's third-party cloud infrastructure provider, Carrowmere Cloud. Scheduled maintenance windows affecting the `oms-mtn-prod` tenant will continue to be coordinated outside of Customer's peak hospital replenishment dispatch hours (04:00 to 09:00 Mountain Time, Monday through Saturday) in accordance with the standard operational notifications configured in the Service administration console.

**5.2 Entire Modification; Counterparts.** This Renewal Order Form, drafted on 9/8/26 and executed on 9/24/26, constitutes the complete and exclusive statement of the mutual understanding of the Parties with respect to the 2026–2027 renewal period and supersedes all prior written or oral proposals, quotes, or discussions relating to said renewal period. This Renewal Order Form may be executed in two or more counterparts, each of which shall be deemed an original, and all of which together shall constitute one and the same instrument. Electronic signatures shall have the same legal effect as original ink signatures.

**5.3 Deal Desk Processing Note.** Internal routing record: Order packet generated on 9/8/26; final redlines regarding facility address descriptions in Section 2.2 cleared by Customer legal counsel on 9/22/26. Forwarded for final signature execution on 9/24/26.

**1.1 Parties.** This Renewal Order Form (this "Renewal Order Form") is entered into by and between **Pemberline Systems** ("Provider"), a corporation having its principal place of business at 400 Mercer Street, Suite 900, Seattle, WA 98109, and **Thornbury Cloth Co.** ("Customer"), formerly known as **Orrin Mills**, a textile manufacturing corporation having its principal operational offices at 1820 Old Loom Highway, Spartanburg, SC 29301. Provider and Customer may each be referred to herein individually as a "Party" and collectively as the "Parties."

**1.2 Corporate Name Change.** The Parties acknowledge that Customer legally changed its corporate name from Orrin Mills to Thornbury Cloth Co. on 1/12/26. All references to Orrin Mills in the underlying agreement and any prior order forms, exhibits, or statements of work between the Parties shall hereafter be deemed to refer to Thornbury Cloth Co. without interruption of rights, obligations, or liabilities.

**1.3 Governing Agreement.** This Renewal Order Form is governed by and incorporated into the earlier agreement previously executed between Provider and Customer (then operating under the name Orrin Mills) governing the provision of Provider's hosted software-as-a-service offerings (the "Agreement"). This Renewal Order Form amends, supersedes, and replaces the commercial seat allocations and term dates set forth in the earlier paperwork for Customer as of the Effective Date specified herein. In the event of any express conflict between the provisions of this Renewal Order Form and the terms of the Agreement, the provisions of this Renewal Order Form shall prevail solely with respect to the subject matter of the subscription renewal detailed herein.

---

## 2. Dates and Renewal Term

**2.1 Distinction of Dates.** This Renewal Order Form was drafted by Provider on 2/17/26 and is executed and signed by the authorized representatives of both Parties on 2/24/26 (the "Execution Date"). Notwithstanding the Execution Date of 2/24/26, the commercial terms, seat allocations, and fee obligations established under this Renewal Order Form shall not commence until 3/1/26 (the "Effective Date"). Between the Execution Date of 2/24/26 and the Effective Date of 3/1/26, the Parties' rights and obligations shall continue to be governed by the prior order form then in effect under the Agreement.

**2.2 Renewal Term.** The subscription term governed by this Renewal Order Form shall commence at 12:00 a.m. Eastern Time on the Effective Date of 3/1/26 and shall continue in full force and effect through 11:59 p.m. Eastern Time on 2/28/27 (the "Renewal Date" and the end of the current term), unless earlier terminated in accordance with the express termination provisions of the Agreement.

---

## 3. Subscribed Software and Commercial Terms

**3.1 Product Description.** Subject to the terms of the Agreement and timely payment of the applicable fees, Provider grants Customer a non-exclusive, non-transferable right during the Renewal Term to access and use **Pemberline Dock**, Provider's cloud-based yard and dock scheduling software platform, up to the quantity of subscribed seats specified below.

**3.2 Subscription Schedule.** As of the Effective Date of 3/1/26, Customer's subscription under the Agreement is hereby updated and set as follows:

| Subscription Item | Metric | Subscribed Quantity | Price per Seat per Year (USD) | Total Annual Fee (USD) |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| Pemberline Dock (Standard Yard & Dock Scheduling Platform) | Named User Seat | 40 | $1,700.00 | $68,000.00 |

**3.3 Summary of Commercial Terms.** For avoidance of doubt, the terms set by this Renewal Order Form are:
* **Subscribed Seats:** 40
* **Price per Seat per Year (USD):** $1,700
* **Total Annual Subscription Fee (USD):** $68,000
* **Effective Date:** 3/1/26
* **End of Current Term (Renewal Date):** 2/28/27

**3.4 Seat Administration and Reassignment.** Each of the 40 subscribed seats corresponds to a single unique Named User login credential within Customer's Pemberline Dock tenant (`tcc-carolinas-prod`). Named User credentials may not be shared concurrently across multiple individuals or shift desks. Customer's designated system administrators may reassign a Named User seat without additional charge only when an individual permanently leaves Customer's employ, transfers to a role outside yard and shipping operations, or goes on extended leave exceeding thirty (30) consecutive calendar days.

---

## 4. Operational Deployment and Tenant Configuration

**4.1 Covered Facilities.** The 40 subscribed seats under this Renewal Order Form are authorized for deployment across Customer's Carolina textile mill facilities, specifically:
1. **Spartanburg Weaving & Finishing Mill (Plant 1):** North Receiving Yard (Dock Doors N1 through N14, serving raw cotton bale and synthetic yarn flatbeds) and South Greige Goods Shipping Apron (Dock Doors S1 through S10).
2. **Gaffney Dye House & Distribution Annex (Plant 2):** West Chemical & Dye Unloading Bay (Dock Doors W1 through W4, hazardous/bulk tank check-in) and East Finished Bolt Loading Dock (Dock Doors E1 through E8).
3. **Cheraw Auxilliary Roll Storage Yard:** Gatehouse Guard Kiosk 1 and Drop-Lot Staging Lanes A through F.

**4.2 Administrative Tenant Rebranding.** Pursuant to Customer's name change from Orrin Mills to Thornbury Cloth Co. on 1/12/26, Provider's technical operations team shall complete the migration of Customer's automated carrier appointment confirmation emails, SMS driver gate passes, and bill-of-lading dock receipts from the legacy `orrinmills.com` sender header to `scheduling@thornburycloth.com` under Support Ticket #PD-88412 prior to the 3/1/26 Effective Date. The custom report template titled *Daily Greige Roll Dwell & Detention Log (Carolinas)* and the third-shift yard jockey tablet profiles at the Spartanburg gatehouse will remain active without reconfiguration.

---

## 5. Invoicing and Payment Administration

**5.1 Billing Administration.** Provider utilizes its third-party billing and invoicing vendor, **Stoneharrow Billing**, to generate, deliver, and process all invoices associated with this Renewal Order Form. Customer acknowledges that invoices will be issued electronically from the Stoneharrow Billing portal referencing Provider's account receivable ledger.

**5.2 Invoicing Schedule and Remittance.** The Total Annual Subscription Fee of $68,000 USD (representing 40 subscribed seats at $1,700 USD per seat per year) shall be invoiced upon the Effective Date of 3/1/26. All payments shall be remitted in United States Dollars via Automated Clearing House (ACH) or wire transfer to the remittance account specified on the Stoneharrow Billing invoice, referencing Customer Code **TCC** and Order Reference **PEM-ROF-2026-0217-TCC**.

**5.3 Customer Billing Contact.** Invoices and billing notices shall be directed to:

**5.4 Taxes.** The price per seat per year of $1,700 USD is exclusive of any applicable federal, state, local, or municipal sales, use, value-added, or excise taxes. ### 1. Definitions and Scope of Services
**1.1. Hosted Software.** Provider hereby grants to Customer a non-exclusive, non-transferable, worldwide right to access and use the cloud-based yard and dock scheduling software platform known as **Pemberline Dock** (the "Service") during the Term, solely for Customer's internal port drayage, chassis staging, and marine terminal gate scheduling operations.

Permitted Users and Operational Environment.** A "Seat" is defined as an individual named user credential provisioned within the Customer's Pemberline Dock tenant, whether assigned to a marine gate clerk, harbour dispatch coordinator, yard jockey supervisor, or container berth scheduler. **1.3. Hosting Infrastructure.** Customer acknowledges that the Service is hosted on enterprise cloud infrastructure provided by Provider's third-party subcontractor, Carrowmere Cloud. ### 2. Subscription Schedule and Commercial Terms

**2.2. Subscription Fees and Discount.** The standard list price for the Service is **1900** USD per Seat per year. **2.3. Invoicing and Payment Terms.** Provider shall issue the annual subscription invoice upon the Effective Date (1 Mar 2025). # Amendment 2: Pellucid Harbor Logistics pricing

This Amendment 2 ("Amendment") is drafted as of September 14, 2026, and is entered into and executed on September 29, 2026 (the "Execution Date"), by and between Pemberline Systems ("Pemberline"), having its principal place of business at 4100 East Marginal Way, and Pellucid Harbor Logistics ("Customer"), having its principal operational offices at Terminal 4, Berth 12, Port of Galveston, Texas. Pemberline and Customer may each be referred to herein individually as a "Party" and collectively as the "Parties."

## 1. Recitals and Background

**1.1.** Whereas, the Parties previously entered into that certain master subscription agreement and associated order forms (collectively, the "Prior Agreement") pursuant to which Pemberline grants Customer access to and use of Pemberline Dock, a proprietary yard and dock scheduling software platform.

**1.2.** Whereas, Customer utilizes Pemberline Dock across its Gulf Coast port drayage and terminal logistics operations, including without limitation the scheduling of container chassis turnarounds at West Yard Gate 3, reefer plug-in queue management along Doors 14 through 28, and third-shift dispatcher handoffs for inbound coastal vessels.

**1.3.** Whereas, the Parties now desire to modify and amend certain commercial pricing and discount provisions set forth in the Prior Agreement, specifically to establish revised per-seat annual pricing and an updated commercial discount percentage to govern Customer's subscription commencing on the Amendment Effective Date defined below.

**1.4.** Now, therefore, in consideration of the mutual covenants, terms, and conditions set forth herein, and for other good and valuable consideration, the receipt and sufficiency of which are hereby acknowledged, the Parties agree as follows:

## 2. Definitions and Interpretation

**2.1.** Capitalized terms used but not otherwise defined in this Amendment shall have the meanings ascribed to such terms in the Prior Agreement.

**2.2.** "Seat" means an individual named user credential provisioned within the Pemberline Dock production environment for use by Customer's gate clerks, yard jockey coordinators, drayage dispatchers, or terminal supervisors, provided that credentials may not be shared concurrently across multiple individuals on the same shift.

**2.3.** In the event of any conflict, inconsistency, or ambiguity between the terms and conditions of this Amendment and the terms and conditions of the Prior Agreement, the terms and conditions of this Amendment shall control and prevail solely with respect to the subject matter hereof.

## 3. Effective Date vs. Execution Date

**3.1.** The Parties expressly acknowledge and agree that although this Amendment is signed and executed by both Parties on September 29, 2026 (the "Execution Date"), the commercial modifications set forth in Section 4 of this Amendment shall not take effect until March 1, 2027 (the "Amendment Effective Date").

**3.2.** During the interim period between the Execution Date of September 29, 2026, and the Amendment Effective Date of March 1, 2027, the pricing and fee schedules established under the Prior Agreement shall remain in full force and effect without modification.

## 4. Amended Commercial Terms

**4.1.** **Price Per Seat Per Year.** Commencing on the Amendment Effective Date of March 1, 2027, the Prior Agreement is hereby amended such that the net subscription fee for Pemberline Dock shall be Two Thousand Ten United States Dollars ($2,010 USD) per Seat per year.

**4.2.** **Commercial Discount.** The Parties acknowledge and record that the pricing established in Section 4.1 reflects an applied commercial discount of nine percent (9%). This 9% discount supersedes and replaces any prior promotional rate, volume tier reduction, or legacy discount schedule previously set forth in the Prior Agreement.

**4.3.** **Currency and Invoicing.** All monetary amounts stated in this Amendment are denominated in United States Dollars (USD). Invoices referencing the amended pricing set forth in this Section 4 shall be directed to Customer's accounts payable registry at the Port of Galveston terminal office, referencing vendor portal routing code `PHL-AP-DOCK-02`, and shall be issued in accordance with the billing schedule governed by the Prior Agreement.

**5.2.** Nothing in this Amendment shall be construed to alter Customer's obligations regarding gate hardware maintenance, handheld scanner connectivity at Berth 12, or local network availability at Customer's Gulf Coast facilities.

## 6. Ratification and Miscellaneous

**6.1.** **No Other Modifications.** Except as expressly modified and amended by this Amendment, all terms, covenants, representations, and conditions of the Prior Agreement remain unchanged and are hereby ratified, confirmed, and continued in full force and effect.

# Pellucid Harbor Logistics

| Field | Detail |
|---|---|
| Updated | Oct 1st, 2026 |

| Seats | 145 |
| Current owner | Kwame Adjei-Rowe, since Nov 3rd, 2025 |
| Previous owner | Bettina Kroll, until Nov 3rd, 2025 |

## Working picture

Pellucid Harbor moves containers between terminal pickup lanes and off-port staging. Mobile desk starts early; Gulfport afternoon crew inherits the appointment changes. Lots of same-day reshuffling when a container clears later than expected. Dispatch wants the board readable without opening every appointment. Fair complaint.

Main friction: drivers arriving with the original slot printed on their dispatch sheet after the desk has moved it. Yard clerk checks the gate list, driver checks paper, both think the other is wrong. Not really a capacity problem. More a stale-copy problem.

## Current loose ends

- Mobile, door 4: two appointments looked stacked after a reassignment. Ticket DOCK-4827 has screenshots from the morning board. Need the exact sequence, not another screenshot of the final state.
- Gulfport: overnight dispatcher says the “Tomorrow — Terminal Pulls” report sometimes includes completed moves. Checking whether the saved filter was changed or the status update landed late.
- Driver notes: “bring chassis” gets buried below the reference numbers. Asked for one example with the full note intact; recieved a cropped phone photo instead.

## Next up

Kwame Adjei-Rowe to walk through the Mobile reassignment with dispatch. Ten minutes on screen should do it. Ask them to use a dummy appointment, not a live inbound move.

I’ll pull the report filter screenshots and attach them before that call. Also tidy the duplicate site labels — “Gulfport Yard” versus “Gulfport staging.” Same place, confusing in exports.

Quick ops note: avoid shift handoff for screen shares. Everyone dissapears to the gate window. Morning slot better.

| **Created** | 21 Nov 2025 |
| **Status** | Investigating |

### Description
Post-cutover at Terminal 4 (Bayou East), inbound gate events aren't populating on the yard board. Drivers scan in at Lanes 1–3, barrier arm lifts, but Pemberline Dock never registers the `GATE_IN` payload. Yard clerks are manually assigning doors off paper slips. Started right after the 04:00 cutover window on 21 Nov 2025.

### Update Log

**21 Nov 2025 06:42 CST**
Opened ticket after call w/ Raylene (night shift lead at PHL). 14 drayage trucks stuck in `EXPECTED` status despite already sitting at Doors 12–26. Grabbed sample chassis IDs (`PHLZ-409182`, `TRLU-882104`) to trace.

**21 Nov 2025 07:15 CST**
Checked ingest logs. Payloads from the terminal OCR rig are hitting the endpoint, throwing `422 Unprocessable Entity`. Looks like the new terminal controller sends lane IDs as `T4-LN01` instead of the legacy `LN1` string. Dock parser drops the whole event when lane lookup fails.

**21 Nov 2025 08:05 CST**
Pinged Odile Brandt at Carrowmere Cloud just to rule out edge gateway caching from the maintenance window—she confirmed traffic is passing thru clean, def an app-side mapping mismatch on our end.

**21 Nov 2025 08:30 CST**
Uploaded hotfix alias table to staging (`t4_lane_map_v2.json`). Tested w/ three replay payloads from 05:30; all flipped to `YARD_CHECKED` cleanly. Waiting on PHL local IT to approve prod push before the 10:00 vessel discharge rush starts.

---

type: deal
