# Master Subscription Agreement: Pemberline Systems and Quarrendon Freight Lines

**Document Control:** Drafted 3/10/25 | Executed 3/28/25 | Effective Date 4/1/25

This Master Subscription Agreement (this "Agreement") is drafted as of 3/10/25, executed by the duly authorized representatives of the parties on 3/28/25 (the "Execution Date"), and made effective as of 4/1/25 (the "Effective Date"), by and between **Pemberline Systems**, a Delaware corporation having its principal place of business at 440 Commerce Way, Suite 900, Chicago, Illinois ("Pemberline"), and **Quarrendon Freight Lines**, a Minnesota corporation having its principal operational headquarters at 1880 North Terminal Drive, Saint Paul, Minnesota ("Customer" or "QFL"). Pemberline and Customer may each be referred to herein individually as a "Party" and collectively as the "Parties."

## RECITALS

WHEREAS, Pemberline develops, hosts, maintains, and markets a proprietary cloud-based yard and dock scheduling software platform known commercially as Pemberline Dock, designed for freight carriers, distribution centers, and logistics operators;

WHEREAS, Customer operates truckload freight terminals, cross-dock facilities, drop yards, and gatehouse operations across the Upper Midwest and desires to subscribe to Pemberline Dock for the management of its dock doors, trailer staging bays, gate check-ins, and yard jockey dispatches; and

WHEREAS, the Parties desire to establish the terms and conditions under which Pemberline will grant Customer access to the Platform and provide associated support services, as further specified in the Order Schedule attached hereto and incorporated herein by reference.

NOW, THEREFORE, in consideration of the mutual covenants, representations, warranties, and undertakings set forth herein, and for other good and valuable consideration, the receipt and sufficiency of which are hereby acknowledged, the Parties agree as follows:

---

## ARTICLE 1. DEFINITIONS

**1.1 "Affiliate"** means, with respect to any entity, any other entity that directly or indirectly controls, is controlled by, or is under common control with such entity, where "control" means the direct or indirect ownership of more than fifty percent (50%) of the voting securities or equity interests of such entity, or the power to direct the management and policies of such entity.

**1.2 "Authorized User"** means an individual employee, yard clerk, gate guard, dispatcher, terminal manager, or dedicated third-party contractor of Customer who has been assigned a unique username and credential set by Customer to access and use the Platform under a Subscribed Seat.

**1.3 "Confidential Information"** has the meaning set forth in Section 8.1 of this Agreement.

**1.4 "Customer Data"** means all electronic data, text, records, carrier bills of lading numbers, tractor and trailer identifiers, seal numbers, driver check-in logs, dock door schedules, yard spot maps, Detention and Demurrage timestamps, and other operational information submitted, uploaded, imported, or transmitted by or on behalf of Customer or its Authorized Users into the Platform.

**1.5 "Documentation"** means the user manuals, release notes, administrator guides, API specifications, and online help files published by Pemberline from time to time and made generally available to subscribers of Pemberline Dock.

**1.6 "Effective Date"** means 4/1/25, which is the date on which the subscription rights, operational access, and service level obligations under this Agreement commence, distinct from the Execution Date of 3/28/25 on which the Parties signed this Agreement.

**1.7 "Order Schedule"** means the initial ordering document attached hereto as Schedule A, and any subsequent written ordering document executed by both Parties that references this Agreement.

**1.8 "Platform"** means the hosted, multi-tenant software-as-a-service application known as Pemberline Dock, including its web-based dispatcher console, gatehouse kiosk view, carrier self-scheduling portal, yard spotter task module, and standard application programming interfaces (APIs), as updated or modified by Pemberline from time to time in accordance with this Agreement.

**1.9 "Subscribed Seat"** means a single named-user license provisioned within the Platform for one (1) Authorized User. Each Subscribed Seat is specific to a designated individual and may not be shared concurrently among multiple personnel across shifts except as expressly permitted in Section 2.3.

**1.10 "Support Services"** means the technical support, maintenance, bug fixing, and operational assistance provided by Pemberline in accordance with the Tier 2 service level commitments described in Article 5.

---

## ARTICLE 2. SUBSCRIPTION GRANT AND SEATS

**2.1 Provision of Access.** Subject to the terms and conditions of this Agreement and Customer's timely payment of all applicable Fees, Pemberline hereby grants to Customer a non-exclusive, non-transferable (except as permitted under Article 17), non-sublicensable, worldwide right during the active period of this Agreement to access and use the Platform and Documentation solely for Customer's internal business operations in managing its freight terminals, yards, and loading docks.

**2.2 Subscribed Seats.** As of the Effective Date (4/1/25), Customer subscribes to exactly one hundred forty (140) Subscribed Seats of Pemberline Dock. Customer may allocate these 140 Subscribed Seats across its operational terminals, including its Saint Paul hub, Duluth yard, Eau Claire cross-dock, and Des Moines relay station, at the discretion of Customer's system administrators.

**2.3 Seat Assignment and Reassignment.** Each of the 140 Subscribed Seats must be tied to a unique individual identity (using corporate email address or employee badge ID) within the Platform's identity management directory. Customer may not configure generic, shared, or role-based credentials (such as "gatehouse1@qfl.example" or "nightdispatch@qfl.example") to allow multiple individuals on rotating shifts to utilize a single Subscribed Seat. Notwithstanding the foregoing, Customer may permanently reassign a Subscribed Seat from one individual to another without penalty when an Authorized User terminates employment, transfers out of yard or dock operations, or goes on extended leave exceeding fourteen (14) consecutive calendar days.

**2.4 Seat Audits and True-Up.** Pemberline's Platform includes automated seat-count enforcement that prevents the provisioning of active credentials beyond the 140 Subscribed Seats unless an administrator with purchasing authority initiates an expansion request. If Customer requires additional seats during an active period, Customer may order additional Subscribed Seats in minimum blocks of five (5) seats by executing an addendum to the Order Schedule. Any mid-period seat additions shall be priced at the discounted net rate set forth in Section 3.1, prorated for the remainder of the then-current period.

**2.5 Reservation of Rights.** This Agreement is a subscription agreement for access to hosted software services and is not a sale of software or intellectual property. Customer acknowledges that it is obtaining only a limited right to access and use the Platform as hosted by Pemberline, and that irrespective of any use of the words "purchase," "sale," or "seat" hereunder, no ownership rights are being conveyed to Customer under this Agreement.

---

## ARTICLE 3. FEES AND PRICING

**3.1 Subscription Fees.** In consideration for the provision of the Platform and the Tier 2 Support Services, Customer shall pay Pemberline the annual subscription fees specified in this Section 3.1 and Schedule A (the "Fees"). The standard list price for Pemberline Dock is one thousand eight hundred fifty United States Dollars ($1,850.00 USD) per Subscribed Seat per year. Under this Agreement, Pemberline grants Customer a contractual discount of twelve percent (12%) off the standard list price, resulting in a net discounted price of one thousand six hundred twenty-eight United States Dollars ($1,628.00 USD) per Subscribed Seat per year.

**3.2 Total Annual Commitment.** Based on the subscription of 140 Subscribed Seats at the list price of $1,850.00 USD per seat per year ($259,000.00 USD gross annual value), less the twelve percent (12%) discount ($31,080.00 USD annual discount), Customer's total net annual subscription Fee for the initial twelve-month period beginning on 4/1/25 and ending on 3/31/26 is two hundred twenty-seven thousand nine hundred twenty United States Dollars ($227,920.00 USD).

**3.3 Non-Cancelable and Non-Refundable.** Except as expressly provided in Section 11.3 (Warranty Remedies), Section 12.1 (Intellectual Property Infringement Mitigation), or Section 16.2 (Termination for Cause by Customer), all Fees are non-cancelable and non-refundable once invoiced. Customer may not reduce its commitment below 140 Subscribed Seats during any active period of this Agreement. No refunds or credits will be issued for partial use, underutilization of the 140 Subscribed Seats, or seasonal reductions in freight volume at Customer's terminals.

**3.4 Taxes.** All Fees stated herein are exclusive of any federal, state, local, municipal, or foreign sales, use, value-added, excise, gross receipts, or other taxes, duties, or governmental assessments ("Taxes"). Customer is solely responsible for paying all Taxes associated with its purchases hereunder, other than taxes assessed on Pemberline's net income, property, or payroll. If Pemberline is legally required to collect and remit Taxes on Customer's behalf, such Taxes will be itemized separately on the applicable invoice unless Customer provides a valid, properly executed tax exemption certificate prior to invoicing.

---

## ARTICLE 4. INVOICING AND PAYMENT TERMS

**4.1 Invoicing Schedule.** Pemberline (either directly or through its designated billing service provider) shall issue an annual invoice for the total net annual Fee of $227,920.00 USD on or promptly following the Effective Date of 4/1/25. For any subsequent periods, Pemberline shall issue the annual invoice at least thirty (30) calendar days prior to the commencement of such period. Invoices for additional Subscribed Seats added mid-period pursuant to Section 2.4 shall be issued upon provisioning of such seats.

**4.2 Payment Terms.** All undisputed invoices are due and payable in full within forty-five (45) calendar days from the date of the invoice ("Net 45"). All payments shall be made in United States Dollars ($ USD) via Automated Clearing House (ACH) electronic funds transfer or wire transfer to the bank account designated on the invoice. Customer shall bear any wire transfer fees assessed by its originating financial institution.

**4.3 Disputed Invoices.** If Customer in good faith disputes any portion of an invoice, Customer must notify Pemberline's finance department in writing within twenty (20) calendar days of the invoice date, specifying the invoice number, the exact dollar amount in dispute, and a reasonably detailed explanation with supporting documentation for the basis of the dispute. Customer shall timely pay all undisputed portions of the invoice within the Net 45 payment window. The Parties shall work together in good faith to resolve any billing dispute within fifteen (15) business days of Pemberline's receipt of the dispute notice.

**4.4 Late Payments.** Any undisputed amount not received by Pemberline within the Net 45 payment period shall accrue late interest at the rate of one and one-half percent (1.5%) per month, or the maximum rate permitted by applicable law, whichever is lower, calculated from the forty-sixth (46th) day following the invoice date until the date paid in full. In addition to late interest, if an undisputed invoice remains unpaid more than fifteen (15) calendar days past its Net 45 due date, Pemberline shall have the right to exercise its suspension remedies under Article 15.

**4.5 Purchase Orders.** If Customer requires a purchase order number to be referenced on invoices for its internal accounting procedures, Customer shall provide such purchase order number upon execution of this Agreement on 3/28/25. Any pre-printed or standard terms and conditions contained on or referenced by any Customer purchase order, vendor portal registration form, or remittance advice are hereby rejected in their entirety and shall be null, void, and of no legal force or effect, even if signed or acknowledged by Pemberline for administrative convenience.

---

## ARTICLE 5. SUPPORT AND SERVICE LEVELS

**5.1 Support Tier Assignment.** During the active period of this Agreement, Pemberline shall provide Customer with **Tier 2** Support Services for the Platform. Tier 2 Support Services are included in the annual subscription Fees set forth in Article 3 at no additional charge.

**5.2 Tier 2 Channels and Hours.** Under the Tier 2 support plan, Customer's designated system administrators (up to six (6) named individuals appointed by Customer's Director of Yard Operations) may submit support tickets via Pemberline's web-based support portal and by direct telephone hotline.
(a) **Severity 1 (Critical Yard Outage):** Telephone and portal support available twenty-four (24) hours per day, seven (7) days per week, three hundred sixty-five (365) days per year (24x7x365). A Severity 1 issue is defined as a complete inability of Authorized Users at one or more terminals to access the Platform, or a failure of core gate check-in or dock door assignment functions with no operational workaround, resulting in physical truck queues at terminal gates.
(b) **Severity 2 (Major Operational Degradation):** Support coverage available Monday through Saturday, 5:00 AM to 11:00 PM Central Time. A Severity 2 issue is defined as a substantial impairment of primary features (such as yard jockey task dispatch latency, failure of EDI 214 status message transmission, or carrier portal booking failure) where core yard operations can continue via manual workaround within the Platform.
(c) **Severity 3 (Minor Feature Issue):** Support coverage available Monday through Friday, 7:00 AM to 7:00 PM Central Time, excluding US federal holidays. A Severity 3 issue is defined as a non-critical malfunction, reporting discrepancy, or user interface defect that has minimal impact on daily dock scheduling.
(d) **Severity 4 (Cosmetic or Inquiry):** Support coverage available Monday through Friday, 8:00 AM to 5:00 PM Central Time. A Severity 4 issue includes general "how-to" configuration questions, documentation requests, or cosmetic enhancement requests.

**5.3 Tier 2 Target Response Times.** Under the Tier 2 SLA, Pemberline commits to the following initial human response times from the moment a ticket is logged in the support portal or received via the emergency telephone hotline:
* **Severity 1:** Within thirty (30) minutes, with continuous engineering engagement and status updates every sixty (60) minutes until service is restored.
* **Severity 2:** Within two (2) hours during covered hours, with status updates every four (4) hours.
* **Severity 3:** Within eight (8) business hours.
* **Severity 4:** Within two (2) business days.

**5.4 Platform Availability Commitment.** Under the Tier 2 SLA, Pemberline shall maintain a Monthly Uptime Percentage for the production instance of the Platform of at least ninety-nine and five-tenths percent (99.5%), measured across each calendar month. "Monthly Uptime Percentage" is calculated by subtracting from 100% the percentage of total minutes in the calendar month during which the Platform experienced Unscheduled Downtime.

**5.5 Exclusions from Unscheduled Downtime.** Unscheduled Downtime does not include unavailability resulting from: (a) Scheduled Maintenance windows occurring between Saturday 11:00 PM Central Time and Sunday 3:00 AM Central Time, provided Pemberline gives at least forty-eight (48) hours' prior electronic notice via the Platform status page; (b) Force Majeure Events as defined in Section 19.3; (c) failures of Customer's local yard Wi-Fi networks, cellular data terminals mounted in yard spotter cabs, barcode scanners, RFID gate readers, or local internet service providers; (d) interruptions caused by third-party transportation management systems (TMS) or warehouse management systems (WMS) integrated by Customer via API; or (e) suspension of Customer's access pursuant to Article 15.

**5.6 Service Credits.** If Pemberline fails to meet the 99.5% Monthly Uptime Percentage under the Tier 2 SLA in any given calendar month, Customer shall be eligible to receive a Service Credit applied against its next invoice, calculated as a percentage of one-twelfth (1/12th) of the net annual subscription Fee ($18,993.33 USD monthly equivalent), as follows:
* Monthly Uptime Percentage between 99.00% and 99.49%: Five percent (5%) credit.
* Monthly Uptime Percentage between 98.00% and 98.99%: Ten percent (10%) credit.
* Monthly Uptime Percentage below 98.00%: Twenty percent (20%) credit.
To receive a Service Credit, Customer must submit a written request within thirty (30) calendar days following the end of the calendar month in which the Unscheduled Downtime occurred. Service Credits are Customer's sole and exclusive financial remedy for any failure to meet the Tier 2 availability metrics, provided that if the Monthly Uptime Percentage falls below 97.00% for three (3) consecutive calendar months, Customer may treat such failure as a material breach under Section 16.2.

---

## ARTICLE 6. CUSTOMER DATA

**6.1 Ownership of Customer Data.** As between the Parties, Customer retains all right, title, and interest (including all intellectual property rights) in and to all Customer Data. Pemberline acquires no rights in Customer Data other than the limited right to host, process, transmit, display, and back up Customer Data as necessary to provide the Platform and Tier 2 Support Services in accordance with this Agreement.

**6.2 License to Process.** Customer grants Pemberline and its authorized cloud infrastructure subprocessors a non-exclusive, worldwide, royalty-free license during the active period of this Agreement to host, copy, transmit, index, and display Customer Data solely for the purposes of operating, maintaining, securing, and troubleshooting the Platform on Customer's behalf and enabling Customer's designated carrier partners to view and book dock appointments at Customer's facilities as configured by Customer.

**6.3 Responsibility for Customer Data.** Customer is solely responsible for the accuracy, quality, integrity, and legality of all Customer Data and the means by which Customer acquires Customer Data. Customer represents and warrants that it has provided all necessary notices and obtained all required consents from drivers, third-party drayage carriers, and employees whose personal contact details (such as mobile phone numbers used for SMS dock-ready alerts) are entered into the Platform. Customer shall not upload into the Platform any payment card industry (PCI) data, Social Security numbers, government-issued driver's license photographs, medical certification records, or hazardous materials security plans regulated under 49 CFR Part 172 Subpart I (other than standard UN/NA four-digit hazard class placarding codes necessary for yard segregation rules).

**6.4 Aggregated Telemetry.** Notwithstanding anything to the contrary herein, Pemberline may collect and analyze de-identified, anonymized statistical metadata regarding Platform performance, system load, query execution speeds, and general feature utilization ("Aggregated Telemetry"), provided that such Aggregated Telemetry does not identify Customer, any Authorized User, any specific freight terminal location, any shipping customer of QFL, or any individual driver, and cannot be reverse-engineered to reveal any Customer Data.

**6.5 Data Export and Retrieval.** At any time during the active period of this Agreement, Customer may export its Customer Data (including historical gate logs, dock turnaround metrics, and carrier scorecards) in standard comma-separated values (CSV) or JSON format using the Platform's self-service reporting and API tools. Upon the conclusion or termination of this Agreement for any reason, Pemberline shall maintain Customer Data in a read-only exportable state for thirty (30) calendar days to allow Customer to complete a final extraction. Following such thirty (30) day window, Pemberline shall permanently delete and overwrite all Customer Data from its active production databases within fifteen (15) calendar days, and from its encrypted backup archives within ninety (90) calendar days in accordance with its standard backup lifecycle rotation.

---

## ARTICLE 7. INFORMATION SECURITY AND PRIVACY

**7.1 Security Program.** Pemberline shall maintain a formal, written information security program that includes administrative, physical, and technical safeguards designed to protect the security, confidentiality, and integrity of Customer Data against unauthorized access, destruction, modification, or disclosure. Such safeguards shall be no less rigorous than accepted industry standards for enterprise B2B software-as-a-service providers, including alignment with AICPA SOC 2 Type II Trust Services Criteria.

**7.2 Technical Controls.** Without limiting the generality of Section 7.1, Pemberline's technical safeguards shall include at a minimum: (a) encryption of all Customer Data in transit over public networks using Transport Layer Security (TLS 1.2 or higher); (b) encryption of all Customer Data at rest in database storage and backup volumes using Advanced Encryption Standard with 256-bit keys (AES-256); (c) logical tenant isolation in the application and database layers to prevent any other customer from accessing Customer Data; (d) support for Security Assertion Markup Language (SAML 2.0) single sign-on (SSO) integration and multi-factor authentication (MFA) for all 140 Subscribed Seats; and (e) role-based access controls (RBAC) allowing Customer to restrict user permissions by terminal location and operational function.

**7.3 Audits and Certifications.** At least once every twelve (12) months, Pemberline shall engage an independent, certified third-party auditing firm to conduct a SOC 2 Type II examination of the controls governing the Platform. Upon Customer's written request (not more than once annually), Pemberline shall provide Customer with a confidential copy of its most recent SOC 2 Type II report and executive summary of its annual third-party penetration test, which shall be treated as Pemberline's Confidential Information under Article 8.

**7.4 Security Incident Notification.** In the event Pemberline confirms an unauthorized acquisition, access, alteration, or disclosure of unencrypted Customer Data residing on Pemberline's systems (a "Security Incident"), Pemberline shall notify Customer without undue delay, and in any event within forty-eight (48) hours of confirmation. Such notice shall be delivered to Customer's primary operational contact and legal department and shall describe the nature of the Security Incident, the categories of Customer Data affected, the root cause (to the extent then known), and the containment and remediation measures taken by Pemberline. Pemberline shall cooperate with Customer's reasonable requests for information necessary for Customer to comply with applicable data breach notification laws.

**7.5 Business Continuity and Disaster Recovery.** Pemberline shall maintain and annually test a disaster recovery and business continuity plan for the Platform. The production environment for Pemberline Dock shall utilize redundant availability zones within the continental United States, configured to achieve a Recovery Point Objective (RPO) of no more than fifteen (15) minutes and a Recovery Time Objective (RTO) of no more than four (4) hours in the event of a catastrophic data center failure.

---

## ARTICLE 8. CONFIDENTIALITY

**8.1 Definition of Confidential Information.** "Confidential Information" means all non-public information disclosed by or on behalf of a Party (the "Disclosing Party") to the other Party (the "Receiving Party"), whether orally, visually, or in writing, that is designated as confidential or that reasonably should be understood to be confidential given the nature of the information and the circumstances of disclosure. Pemberline's Confidential Information includes, without limitation, the Platform's source code, system architecture, non-public API documentation, product roadmaps, SOC 2 audit reports, and the pricing and discount terms of this Agreement (including the 12% discount and net seat pricing). Customer's Confidential Information includes, without limitation, all Customer Data, terminal layouts, freight volume metrics, carrier rate structures, and internal operational procedures.

**8.2 Exclusions.** Confidential Information shall not include any information that the Receiving Party can demonstrate by written records: (a) is or becomes generally known to the public without breach of any obligation owed to the Disclosing Party; (b) was rightfully in the Receiving Party's possession prior to its disclosure by the Disclosing Party without restriction on use or disclosure; (c) is rightfully received from a third party without breach of any confidentiality obligation; or (d) was independently developed by the Receiving Party without reference to or use of the Disclosing Party's Confidential Information.

**8.3 Protection and Use Obligations.** The Receiving Party shall: (a) use the same degree of care to protect the Disclosing Party's Confidential Information that it uses to protect the confidentiality of its own confidential information of like kind, but in no event less than a reasonable standard of care; (b) not use any Confidential Information of the Disclosing Party for any purpose outside the scope of this Agreement; and (c) limit access to the Disclosing Party's Confidential Information to those of its and its Affiliates' employees, contractors, legal counsel, and financial advisors who need such access for purposes consistent with this Agreement and who are bound by confidentiality obligations at least as protective as those set forth herein.

**8.4 Compelled Disclosure.** The Receiving Party may disclose Confidential Information of the Disclosing Party to the extent compelled to do so by a court of competent jurisdiction, subpoena, civil investigative demand, or governmental regulatory body, provided that the Receiving Party gives the Disclosing Party prompt prior written notice of such compelled disclosure (to the extent legally permitted) and provides reasonable assistance, at the Disclosing Party's cost, if the Disclosing Party wishes to contest the disclosure or seek a protective order.

**8.5 Injunctive Relief.** Each Party acknowledges that any actual or threatened breach of this Article 8 may cause irreparable harm to the Disclosing Party for which monetary damages alone would be an inadequate remedy. Accordingly, in addition to any other remedies available at law or in equity, the Disclosing Party shall be entitled to seek immediate injunctive or other equitable relief in a court of competent jurisdiction without the necessity of posting a bond or proving actual monetary damages.

---

## ARTICLE 9. INTELLECTUAL PROPERTY RIGHTS

**9.1 Pemberline Intellectual Property.** As between the Parties, Pemberline owns and retains all right, title, and interest, including all patents, copyrights, trade secrets, trademarks, service marks, and other intellectual property rights, in and to the Platform (Pemberline Dock), the Documentation, all underlying algorithms, heuristics, yard optimization engines, user interface designs, database schemas, and any modifications, enhancements, updates, or derivative works thereof ("Pemberline IP"). Except for the limited access rights expressly granted in Article 2, no rights or licenses in any Pemberline IP are granted to Customer, whether by implication, estoppel, or otherwise.

**9.2 Customer Marks.** Customer retains all right, title, and interest in and to its corporate name ("Quarrendon Freight Lines"), trade names ("QFL" and "Q-Freight"), logos, and trademarks ("Customer Marks"). Customer grants Pemberline a limited, non-exclusive, revocable license during the active period of this Agreement to display Customer Marks solely within the branded carrier self-scheduling portal configured for Customer's instance of the Platform, so that third-party carriers booking dock appointments can identify the facility as operated by Customer. Pemberline shall not use Customer's name or Customer Marks in external press releases, marketing case studies, or public website customer lists without Customer's prior written consent in each instance.

**9.3 Feedback.** If Customer or any Authorized User voluntarily provides suggestions, enhancement requests, workflow recommendations, or other feedback regarding the features or operation of Pemberline Dock ("Feedback"), Customer hereby grants Pemberline a perpetual, irrevocable, worldwide, royalty-free, fully paid-up license to use, incorporate, modify, and commercialize such Feedback in the Platform or other Pemberline products without any obligation, attribution, or compensation to Customer, provided that Pemberline shall not include any Customer Confidential Information or Customer Data in any product update resulting from such Feedback.

---

## ARTICLE 10. ACCEPTABLE USE AND RESTRICTIONS

**10.1 Use Restrictions.** Customer shall not, and shall not permit any Authorized User, contractor, or third party to:
(a) license, sublicense, sell, resell, rent, lease, transfer, assign, distribute, time-share, or otherwise commercially exploit or make the Platform available to any third party, other than providing limited portal access to third-party carriers delivering to or picking up freight from Customer's own terminals;
(b) copy, modify, adapt, translate, or create derivative works based upon the Platform or the Documentation;
(c) reverse engineer, decompile, disassemble, or otherwise attempt to derive the source code, object code, or underlying algorithmic structure of the Platform, except to the limited extent such restriction is expressly prohibited by applicable law;
(d) access the Platform or Documentation in order to build a competitive yard management, dock scheduling, or gate automation product or service, or to benchmark the Platform's availability, performance, or functionality for competitive purposes;
(e) conduct any unannounced automated vulnerability scans, load tests, denial-of-service simulations, or penetration tests against the Platform's multi-tenant production environment without Pemberline's prior written authorization and coordination;
(f) circumvent or disable any security control, rate limit, or seat-counting mechanism built into the Platform to enforce the limit of 140 Subscribed Seats; or
(g) use the Platform to store or transmit any malicious code, viruses, worms, Trojan horses, ransomware, or unlawful material.

**10.2 Customer Responsibilities.** Customer is responsible for all activities conducted under its 140 Subscribed Seats and for ensuring that its Authorized Users comply with the terms of this Agreement. Customer shall promptly notify Pemberline if it becomes aware of any unauthorized access to any Authorized User credential or any violation of this Article 10. Customer is solely responsible for procuring and maintaining the workstation hardware, ruggedized yard tablets, handheld barcode scanners, gate kiosks, and local network connectivity at its facilities necessary to connect to the Platform.

---

## ARTICLE 11. REPRESENTATIONS, WARRANTIES, AND DISCLAIMERS

**11.1 Mutual Representations.** Each Party represents and warrants to the other that: (a) it is duly organized, validly existing, and in good standing under the laws of its jurisdiction of incorporation; (b) it has full corporate power and authority to enter into this Agreement on the Execution Date of 3/28/25 and to perform its obligations hereunder; (c) the individual signing this Agreement on its behalf is duly authorized to do so; and (d) this Agreement constitutes the legal, valid, and binding obligation of such Party, enforceable against it in accordance with its terms.

**11.2 Pemberline Warranties.** Pemberline warrants to Customer that during the active period of this Agreement:
(a) **Performance Warranty:** The Platform will perform in all material respects in accordance with the specifications set forth in the Documentation under normal operational use;
(b) **No Diminution of Functionality:** Pemberline will not materially decrease the core overall functionality of the Platform or the scope of the Tier 2 Support Services during any paid period; and
(c) **Malicious Code Warranty:** Pemberline will use industry-standard commercial antivirus and malware scanning utilities to ensure that the Platform as delivered by Pemberline does not contain any viruses, worms, time bombs, backdoors, or other code designed to disrupt, disable, or harm Customer's systems or Customer Data.

**11.3 Warranty Remedies.** For any breach of the warranties set forth in Section 11.2, Customer shall promptly notify Pemberline in writing detailing the non-conformity. Pemberline shall, at its own expense, use commercially reasonable efforts to correct the non-conformity within thirty (30) calendar days of receiving such notice. If Pemberline is unable to correct a material non-conformity within such thirty (30) day period, Customer may, as its sole and exclusive remedy for breach of Section 11.2, terminate this Agreement upon written notice to Pemberline and receive a pro-rata refund of any prepaid subscription Fees covering the remainder of the current period following the effective date of such termination.

**11.4 Disclaimer of Implied Warranties.** EXCEPT FOR THE EXPRESS WARRANTIES SET FORTH IN THIS ARTICLE 11, THE PLATFORM, DOCUMENTATION, AND TIER 2 SUPPORT SERVICES ARE PROVIDED strictly ON AN "AS IS" AND "AS AVAILABLE" BASIS. PEMBERLINE HEREBY DISCLAIMS ALL OTHER WARRANTIES, WHETHER EXPRESS, IMPLIED, STATUTORY, OR OTHERWISE, INCLUDING ANY IMPLIED WARRANTIES OF MERCHANTABILITY, FITNESS FOR A PARTICULAR PURPOSE, TITLE, AND NON-INFRINGEMENT, AND ANY WARRANTIES ARISING OUT OF COURSE OF DEALING OR USAGE OF TRADE. PEMBERLINE DOES NOT WARRANT THAT THE PLATFORM WILL OPERATE TOTALLY UNINTERRUPTED OR ERROR-FREE, OR THAT THE USE OF THE PLATFORM WILL PREVENT ALL PHYSICAL ACCIDENTS, TRAILER COLLISIONS, CARGO DELAYS, OR DETENTION CHARGES WITHIN CUSTOMER'S YARDS.

---

## ARTICLE 12. INDEMNIFICATION

**12.1 Indemnification by Pemberline.** Pemberline shall defend Customer, its Affiliates, and their respective officers, directors, and employees ("Customer Indemnitees") against any claim, demand, suit, or proceeding made or brought against a Customer Indemnitee by an unaffiliated third party alleging that the use of the Platform as permitted hereunder infringes or misappropriates such third party's valid United States or Canadian patent, copyright, trademark, or trade secret ("IP Claim"), and shall indemnify and hold harmless the Customer Indemnitees from any damages, court-ordered awards, reasonable attorneys' fees, and settlement amounts finally awarded against the Customer Indemnitees or agreed to in settlement by Pemberline resulting from such IP Claim.

**12.2 Mitigation of IP Claims.** If the use of the Platform by Customer becomes, or in Pemberline's reasonable opinion is likely to become, the subject of an IP Claim, Pemberline may, at its sole option and expense: (a) procure for Customer the right to continue using the Platform under the terms of this Agreement; (b) replace or modify the affected component of the Platform so that it becomes non-infringing while maintaining substantially equivalent yard and dock scheduling functionality; or (c) if neither option (a) nor (b) is commercially practicable despite Pemberline's reasonable efforts, terminate this Agreement upon thirty (30) days' written notice and refund to Customer any prepaid subscription Fees prorated for the remainder of the unexpired period following the effective date of termination.

**12.3 Exclusions from Pemberline Indemnity.** Pemberline shall have no liability or obligation under Section 12.1 with respect to any IP Claim to the extent arising from: (a) modification of the Platform by anyone other than Pemberline or its authorized contractors; (b) use of the Platform in combination with third-party hardware, yard sensors, or software not provided or specified in the Documentation by Pemberline, where the Platform alone would not be infringing; (c) Customer's continued use of an superseded version or configuration of the Platform after Pemberline has made available a non-infringing update at no additional charge and notified Customer to implement it; or (d) Customer Data or Customer's specific custom business rules configured by Customer.

**12.4 Indemnification by Customer.** Customer shall defend Pemberline, its Affiliates, and their respective officers, directors, and employees ("Pemberline Indemnitees") against any claim, demand, suit, or proceeding made or brought against a Pemberline Indemnitee by an unaffiliated third party: (a) alleging that the Customer Data or Customer Marks, or Pemberline's processing thereof in accordance with this Agreement, infringes or misappropriates the intellectual property or privacy rights of a third party or violates applicable law; or (b) arising out of any physical bodily injury, death, or tangible property damage (including tractor, trailer, dock door, or cargo damage) occurring at Customer's freight terminals or yards, except to the extent caused by Pemberline's gross negligence or willful misconduct; and Customer shall indemnify and hold harmless the Pemberline Indemnitees from any damages, court-ordered awards, reasonable attorneys' fees, and settlement amounts finally awarded against the Pemberline Indemnitees or agreed to in settlement by Customer resulting from such claim.

**12.5 Indemnification Procedure.** The obligations of each indemnifying Party ("Indemnitor") under this Article 12 are conditioned upon the Party seeking indemnification ("Indemnitee"): (a) promptly giving the Indemnitor written notice of the third-party claim (provided that failure to give prompt notice shall only relieve the Indemnitor of its obligations to the extent the Indemnitor is materially prejudiced thereby); (b) granting the Indemnitor sole control of the defense and settlement of the claim (except that the Indemnitor may not settle any claim unless the settlement unconditionally releases the Indemnitee of all liability and does not admission of fault or payment by the Indemnitee); and (c) providing the Indemnitor, at the Indemnitor's expense, with all reasonable assistance, information, and authority necessary to defend or settle the claim.

---

## ARTICLE 13. LIMITATION OF LIABILITY

**13.1 Exclusion of Consequential Damages.** TO THE MAXIMUM EXTENT PERMITTED BY APPLICABLE LAW, IN NO EVENT SHALL EITHER PARTY OR ITS AFFILIATES HAVE ANY LIABILITY ARISING OUT OF OR RELATED TO THIS AGREEMENT FOR ANY INDIRECT, INCIDENTAL, SPECIAL, CONSEQUENTIAL, EXEMPLARY, OR PUNITIVE DAMAGES, OR FOR ANY LOST PROFITS, LOST REVENUE, LOSS OF GOODWILL, BUSINESS INTERRUPTION, FREIGHT DETENTION OR DEMURRAGE PENALTIES, OR SUPPLY CHAIN DELAY COSTS, HOWEVER CAUSED AND UNDER ANY THEORY OF LIABILITY (WHETHER IN CONTRACT, TORT, STRICT LIABILITY, OR OTHERWISE), EVEN IF SUCH PARTY HAS BEEN ADVISED OF THE POSSIBILITY OF SUCH DAMAGES OR IF A REMEDY OTHERWISE FAILS OF ITS ESSENTIAL PURPOSE.

**13.2 General Liability Cap.** EXCEPT FOR EXCLUDED CLAIMS (DEFINED IN SECTION 13.3) AND SUPER-CAP CLAIMS (DEFINED IN SECTION 13.4), IN NO EVENT SHALL THE AGGREGATE, CUMULATIVE LIABILITY OF EITHER PARTY TOGETHER WITH ALL OF ITS AFFILIATES ARISING OUT OF OR RELATED TO THIS AGREEMENT EXCEED THE TOTAL NET SUBSCRIPTION FEES ACTUALLY PAID OR PAYABLE BY CUSTOMER TO PEMBERLINE UNDER THIS AGREEMENT DURING THE TWELVE (12) MONTH PERIOD IMMEDIATELY PRECEDING THE EVENT GIVING RISE TO LIABILITY (WHICH FOR THE INITIAL PERIOD EQUALS $227,920.00 USD).

**13.3 Super-Cap for Data Breach and Confidentiality.** FOR ANY CLAIMS ARISING OUT OF A PARTY'S BREACH OF ITS CONFIDENTIALITY OBLIGATIONS UNDER ARTICLE 8 OR PEMBERLINE'S BREACH OF ITS SECURITY OBLIGATIONS UNDER ARTICLE 7 RESULTING IN AN UNAUTHORIZED DISCLOSURE OF CUSTOMER DATA ("SUPER-CAP CLAIMS"), THE AGGREGATE, CUMULATIVE LIABILITY OF THE BREACHING PARTY SHALL NOT EXCEED TWO TIMES (2X) THE TOTAL NET SUBSCRIPTION FEES PAID OR PAYABLE BY CUSTOMER UNDER THIS AGREEMENT DURING THE TWELVE (12) MONTH PERIOD IMMEDIATELY PRECEDING THE EVENT GIVING RISE TO LIABILITY (WHICH FOR THE INITIAL PERIOD EQUALS $455,840.00 USD).

**13.4 Excluded Claims.** THE LIMITATIONS SET FORTH IN SECTIONS 13.2 AND 13.3 SHALL NOT APPLY TO: (a) A PARTY'S INDEMNIFICATION OBLIGATIONS UNDER ARTICLE 12; (b) CUSTOMER'S OBLIGATION TO PAY UNDISPUTED FEES OWED UNDER ARTICLES 3 AND 4; (c) CUSTOMER'S BREACH OF THE LICENSE RESTRICTIONS IN SECTION 10.1; OR (d) LIABILITY ARISING FROM A PARTY'S GROSS NEGLIGENCE, WILLFUL MISCONDUCT, OR FRAUD ("EXCLUDED CLAIMS").

---

## ARTICLE 14. INSURANCE

**14.1 Required Coverage.** During the entire active period of this Agreement, Pemberline shall, at its own cost and expense, procure and maintain in full force and effect insurance policies with financially sound and reputable insurance carriers rated at least "A- VII" by A.M. Best, with minimum coverage limits as follows:
(a) **Commercial General Liability:** Not less than One Million Dollars ($1,000,000 USD) per occurrence and Two Million Dollars ($2,000,000 USD) in the annual aggregate, covering bodily injury, property damage, personal injury, and contractual liability;
(b) **Technology Errors & Omissions and Cyber Liability Insurance:** Not less than Five Million Dollars ($5,000,000 USD) per claim and in the annual aggregate, covering professional software errors and omissions, network security failures, privacy liability, data breach response costs, and regulatory defense expenses;
(c) **Workers' Compensation and Employer's Liability:** Workers' Compensation insurance in accordance with applicable statutory limits for all states in which Pemberline employs personnel, and Employer's Liability insurance with limits of not less than One Million Dollars ($1,000,000 USD) per accident or disease; and
(d) **Umbrella / Excess Liability:** Not less than Three Million Dollars ($3,000,000 USD) per occurrence and in the annual aggregate, providing excess coverage over the underlying Commercial General Liability and Employer's Liability policies.

**14.2 Certificates of Insurance.** Upon Customer's written request following the Execution Date of 3/28/25, Pemberline shall furnish Customer with standard ACORD Certificates of Insurance evidencing the coverages required under Section 14.1. Such policies shall not be canceled or materially reduced below the required limits without Pemberline providing Customer at least thirty (30) days' prior written notice.

---

## ARTICLE 15. SUSPENSION OF SERVICES

**15.1 Suspension for Non-Payment.** If any undisputed invoice rendered by Pemberline remains unpaid more than fifteen (15) calendar days after the Net 45 payment due date (i.e., sixty (60) calendar days from the invoice date), Pemberline may provide Customer with a formal written notice of delinquency. If Customer fails to remit full payment of the overdue undisputed balance within ten (10) business days of receiving such delinquency notice, Pemberline may temporarily suspend Customer's and its Authorized Users' access to the Platform until all overdue undisputed amounts (including applicable late interest under Section 4.4) are paid in full.

**15.2 Emergency Security Suspension.** Pemberline may immediately suspend access to any individual Subscribed Seat or API integration endpoint without prior notice if Pemberline reasonably determines in good faith that: (a) the credential or endpoint is being used to launch a denial-of-service attack, inject malicious code, or compromise the security or multi-tenant integrity of the Platform; or (b) Customer's use of the Platform is in active violation of applicable law. In any such emergency suspension, Pemberline shall: (i) narrow the suspension to the minimum number of Subscribed Seats or endpoints necessary to resolve the threat; (ii) notify Customer's Director of Yard Operations within two (2) hours of the suspension; and (iii) promptly restore access as soon as the security vulnerability or unauthorized activity is remediated.

---

## ARTICLE 16. AGREEMENT PERIOD AND CONTINUATION ELECTIONS

**16.1 Initial Period and Succeeding Periods.** Although executed by the Parties on 3/28/25, the operational period of this Agreement commences on the Effective Date of 4/1/25 and remains in full force and effect through 3/31/26 (the "Initial Period"). Following 3/31/26, this Agreement shall automatically continue in full force and effect for successive twelve-month periods (each a "Succeeding Period"). Either Party may elect not to continue this Agreement into the next Succeeding Period by delivering a written election against continuation to the other Party at least 120 calendar days prior to the close of the then-current period; if such written election is timely delivered, the active status of this Agreement shall conclude at 11:59 PM Central Time on the final day of the then-current period (being 3/31/26 for the Initial Period) without entering a Succeeding Period.

**16.2 Breach and Insolvency Remedies.** Either Party may bring this Agreement to an immediate close for cause: (a) upon thirty (30) calendar days' written notice to the other Party of a material breach of this Agreement, if such material breach remains uncured at the conclusion of such thirty (30) day cure period; or (b) immediately upon written notice if the other Party becomes the subject of a petition in bankruptcy or any other proceeding relating to insolvency, receivership, liquidation, or assignment for the benefit of creditors that is not dismissed within sixty (60) calendar days.

**16.3 Effect of Conclusion.** Upon the conclusion of this Agreement for any reason: (a) all rights granted to Customer with respect to the 140 Subscribed Seats and the Platform shall immediately cease (subject to the thirty-day data retrieval window in Section 6.5); (b) Customer shall immediately cease all use of the Platform and Documentation; (c) each Receiving Party shall, upon written request, return or destroy the Disclosing Party's Confidential Information in accordance with Article 8; and (d) if this Agreement is brought to a close by Customer due to Pemberline's uncured material breach under Section 16.2(a), Pemberline shall refund to Customer any prepaid subscription Fees prorated for the remainder of the then-current period following the effective date of such action. Conversely, if this Agreement is brought to a close by Pemberline due to Customer's uncured material breach under Section 16.2(a), Customer shall remain obligated to pay all unpaid Fees for the remainder of the then-current period.

**16.4 Survival.** The provisions of Section 3.4 (Taxes), Article 4 (to the extent of unpaid Fees accrued prior to conclusion), Section 6.1 (Ownership of Customer Data), Section 6.4 (Aggregated Telemetry), Section 6.5 (Data Export and Retrieval), Article 8 (Confidentiality), Article 9 (Intellectual Property Rights), Section 11.4 (Disclaimer), Article 12 (Indemnification), Article 13 (Limitation of Liability), Section 16.3 (Effect of Conclusion), this Section 16.4, Article 18 (Notices), and Article 19 (General Provisions) shall survive the conclusion of this Agreement.

---

## ARTICLE 17. ASSIGNMENT AND SUBCONTRACTING

**17.1 Restriction on Assignment.** Neither Party may assign, delegate, or transfer this Agreement, in whole or in part, whether voluntarily or by operation of law, without the prior written consent of the other Party, which consent shall not be unreasonably withheld, conditioned, or delayed.

**17.2 Permitted Assignments.** Notwithstanding Section 17.1, either Party may assign this Agreement in its entirety without the other Party's consent to an Affiliate or in connection with a merger, acquisition, corporate reorganization, or sale of all or substantially all of its stock or assets, provided that: (a) the assigning Party gives the other Party prompt written notice of such assignment; (b) the assignee agrees in writing to be bound by all terms and conditions of this Agreement; and (c) in the case of an assignment by Customer, the assignee is not a direct commercial competitor of Pemberline developing yard or dock scheduling software, and Customer's usage does not exceed the 140 Subscribed Seats without executing an expansion order under Section 2.4. Any attempted assignment in violation of this Article 17 shall be null and void.

**17.3 Subprocessors and Billing Vendors.** Pemberline may utilize third-party infrastructure providers (such as cloud hosting data centers) and administrative vendors (including Stoneharrow Billing for invoice generation and accounts receivable management) in the performance of its obligations hereunder, provided that Pemberline remains fully responsible and liable for the performance of all such subcontractors and their compliance with the confidentiality and security standards set forth in this Agreement.

---

**18.1 Form and Delivery.** All legal notices, elections, permissions, and approvals required or permitted under this Agreement must be in writing and shall be deemed to have been duly given upon: (a) personal delivery; (b) the second business day after deposit with a nationally recognized overnight commercial courier service (such as FedEx or UPS) with tracking confirmation; or (c) the first business day after sending by email (provided that the email is accompanied by a PDF copy of the signed notice, no bounce-back or delivery failure notification is received, and a physical confirmation copy is dispatched via overnight courier within twenty-four (24) hours for any notice under Article 12 or Article 16).

## ARTICLE 19. GENERAL PROVISIONS

**19.1 Governing Law and Venue.** This Agreement and any disputes, claims, or controversies arising out of or relating hereto shall be governed by and construed in accordance with the internal laws of the State of Illinois, without giving effect to any choice or conflict of law provision or rule that would cause the application of the laws of any other jurisdiction. **19.2 Waiver of Jury Trial.** EACH PARTY HEREBY IRREVOCABLY AND UNCONDITIONALLY WAIVES ANY RIGHT IT MAY HAVE TO A TRIAL BY JURY IN RESPECT OF ANY LEGAL ACTION ARISING OUT OF OR RELATING TO THIS AGREEMENT OR THE TRANSACTIONS CONTEMPLATED HEREBY.

**19.3 Force Majeure.** Neither Party shall be liable for any delay or failure to perform its obligations under this Agreement (except for the payment of money owed) to the extent that such delay or failure is caused by an event beyond its reasonable control and occurring without its fault or negligence, including acts of God, earthquakes, floods, tornadoes, blizzards, war, terrorism, riots, embargoes, acts of civil or military authorities, widespread internet backbone outages, or national strikes (each a "Force Majeure Event"), provided that the affected Party gives prompt written notice to the other Party and uses diligent efforts to mitigate the impact and resume performance as soon as practicable.

**19.4 Relationship of the Parties.** The Parties are independent contractors. This Agreement does not create a partnership, franchise, joint venture, agency, fiduciary, or employment relationship between the Parties. Neither Party has any authority to bind or commit the other Party in any respect whatsoever.

**19.5 Export Compliance and Anti-Corruption.** The Platform and Documentation may be subject to export control and economic sanctions laws of the United States. **19.6 Severability and Waiver.** If any provision of this Agreement is held by a court of competent jurisdiction to be invalid, illegal, or unenforceable, that provision shall be modified by the court to the minimum extent necessary to make it enforceable (or, if modification is not possible, severed), and the remaining provisions of this Agreement shall remain in full force and effect. No failure or delay by either Party in exercising any right, power, or remedy under this Agreement shall operate as a waiver of that right, nor shall any single or partial exercise preclude any other or further exercise thereof.

**19.7 Entire Agreement and Amendments.** This Agreement, including Schedule A (Order Schedule) attached hereto, constitutes the entire agreement between the Parties with respect to the subject matter hereof and supersedes all prior and contemporaneous proposals, quotes, negotiations, understandings, and communications, whether oral or written, between the Parties relating to such subject matter (including the initial draft circulated on 3/10/25). No modification, amendment, or waiver of any provision of this Agreement shall be effective unless in writing and signed by duly authorized representatives of both Parties.

**19.8 Counterparts and Electronic Signatures.** This Agreement may be executed in two or more counterparts, each of which shall be deemed an original, but all of which together shall constitute one and the same instrument. Counterparts may be delivered via electronic mail (including PDF) or executed via a recognized electronic signature platform (such as DocuSign), and any counterpart so delivered shall be deemed to have been duly and validly delivered and be valid and effective for all purposes as of the Execution Date of 3/28/25.

# Amendment No. 1 to the Quarrendon Master Subscription Agreement

**Written:** 2025-08-19  
**Drafted:** 2025-08-11  
**Execution Date:** 2025-08-19  
**Effective Date:** 2025-09-01

## 1. Parties and Purpose

This Amendment No. 1 (“Amendment”) is entered into by Pemberline Systems and Quarrendon Freight Lines (each a “Party” and together the “Parties”). This Amendment modifies the earlier master subscription agreement and related subscription paperwork between the Parties concerning Quarrendon Freight Lines’ use of Pemberline Dock (collectively, the “Agreement”).

The Parties intend this Amendment to establish the subscribed seat quantity applicable from the Effective Date. References in this Amendment to the Agreement are generic references to the Parties’ earlier agreement and do not designate a separate or replacement subscription.

## 2. Amendment to Subscribed Seats

Effective 2025-09-01, the subscribed seat quantity for Quarrendon Freight Lines under the Agreement shall be **185 seats**.

The quantity stated in this Section replaces any different subscribed seat quantity appearing in the earlier Agreement or related subscription paperwork for Quarrendon Freight Lines. It shall be the controlling subscribed seat quantity for purposes of administering the Pemberline Dock subscription from the Effective Date.

This Amendment addresses subscribed seats only. It does not establish a separate subscription for any yard, dock, shift, or operating location.

## 3. Execution and Effective Date

The Parties executed this Amendment on **2025-08-19**. The seat amendment set forth in Section 2 takes effect on **2025-09-01**, not on the execution date.

Execution before the Effective Date permits the Parties to prepare their subscription records for the change. Such preparation does not accelerate the Effective Date or apply the amended seat quantity to an earlier period. The distinction between execution and effectiveness shall govern any administrative reference to this Amendment.

## 4. Administrative Implementation

Pemberline Systems shall record the amended quantity against the Quarrendon Freight Lines subscription. Quarrendon Freight Lines shall coordinate its user roster so that personnel administering dock appointments and yard scheduling can identify the subscription to which this Amendment applies.

For implementation purposes, the user roster should distinguish individual users from shared operational labels, including dispatch desk and receiving shift labels. Any roster cleanup undertaken in preparation for the Effective Date is an administrative activity and does not itself modify the Agreement.

## 5. Continuing Effect of Agreement

Except for the subscribed seat quantity expressly amended herein, the Agreement remains unchanged and continues in effect. This Amendment does not restate or replace the remaining provisions of the Agreement.

If a provision of the earlier subscription paperwork conflicts with Section 2 concerning subscribed seat quantity from the Effective Date, Section 2 controls. The Parties shall otherwise read this Amendment together with the Agreement.

## 6. Execution

By signing below, the Parties execute this Amendment on the date shown. Their signatures acknowledge the distinct Effective Date stated above.

**For Pemberline Systems**

Signed: /s/ June Osei-Lark  
Name: June Osei-Lark  
Title: Deal desk and contracts manager  
Date signed: 2025-08-19

**For Quarrendon Freight Lines**

Signed: /s/ Thea Ramaswell  
Name: Thea Ramaswell  
Title: Director of Yard Operations  
Date signed: 2025-08-19

# Amendment No. 2 (DRAFT) to the Quarrendon Master Subscription Agreement

**STATUS: DRAFT — NOT FOR EXECUTION — WATERMARK: WORKING DRAFT (2025-12-03)**  
**Document Reference:** LEG-AMD2-QFL-20251203

> **Internal Deal Desk Note (Remove Prior to External Circulation):**  
> Draft prepared on 2025-12-03 following the mid-morning call with Thea Ramaswell regarding the winter operational rollout at the Duluth and Eau Claire cross-dock facilities. Per company policy, because the commercial adjustment herein sets a fifteen percent (15%) discount off standard per-seat annual rates, final sign-off from Anselm Grieve is required before routing out for signature. Please also ensure Felix Duarte at Stoneharrow Billing is copied on the final ticket once executed so the invoice profile for QFL does not revert to list rate on the next billing run.

---

## AMENDMENT NO. 2 TO MASTER SUBSCRIPTION AGREEMENT

This Amendment No. 2 (the **"Amendment"**), drafted as of 2025-12-03, is entered into by and between **Pemberline Systems**, a corporation having its principal place of business at 400 Mercer Waterway, Suite 900 (hereinafter **"Provider"** or **"Pemberline"**), and **Quarrendon Freight Lines**, a truckload freight carrier operating in the Upper Midwest with operational headquarters at 1880 North Terminal Road (hereinafter **"Customer"**, **"QFL"**, or **"Q-Freight"**). Provider and Customer may each be referred to individually as a **"Party"** and collectively as the **"Parties."**

### RECITALS

**WHEREAS**, Provider and Customer previously entered into that certain Master Subscription Agreement (the **"Agreement"**) governing Customer's access to and use of Provider's proprietary yard and dock scheduling software platform known as **Pemberline Dock**, which is licensed and priced on a per-seat, per-year basis;

**WHEREAS**, Customer desires to modify certain commercial terms applicable to its subscription for Pemberline Dock and to memorialize specific operational protocols relating to yard gate check-ins, dock door assignments, and carrier scheduling across its Upper Midwest terminal network; and

**WHEREAS**, the Parties desire to amend the Agreement on the terms and subject to the conditions set forth herein.

**NOW, THEREFORE**, in consideration of the mutual covenants, terms, and conditions set forth herein, and for other good and valuable consideration, the receipt and sufficiency of which are hereby acknowledged, the Parties agree as follows:

---

### 1. DEFINITIONS AND INTERPRETATION

**1.1.** Capitalized terms used but not otherwise defined in this Amendment shall have the meanings ascribed to such terms in the Agreement.

**1.2.** **"Operational Contact"** means Thea Ramaswell, Director of Yard Operations for Quarrendon Freight Lines, or such successor individual as Customer may designate in writing via notice to Provider's contract management desk.

**1.3.** **"Seat"** means an individual, named user credential authorized by Customer to access or administer the Pemberline Dock platform, whether assigned to a yard jockey, gatehouse clerk, dispatch coordinator, or shift supervisor, billed on a per-seat, per-year basis in accordance with the Agreement.

### 2. COMMERCIAL TERMS AND DISCOUNT STRUCTURE

**2.1. Promotional and Volume Discount Adjustment.** Notwithstanding anything to the contrary in the Agreement or any prior schedule or order form thereto, the Parties hereby agree that the applicable discount rate for Customer's subscription to Pemberline Dock shall be modified and fixed at **fifteen percent (15%)** off Provider's standard per-seat, per-year list price. 

**2.2. Application of Discount.** The 15% discount established in Section 2.1 of this Amendment shall apply to the per-seat, per-year subscription fees invoiced to Customer under the Agreement. Provider shall instruct its third-party billing and invoicing administrator, Stoneharrow Billing, to configure Customer's account profile under identifier code **QFL** to reflect the 15% discount rate upon full execution of this Amendment.

**2.3. Internal Finance Authorization Condition Precedent.** Customer acknowledges that under Provider's internal corporate governance policies, any discount exceeding ten percent (10%) requires the express written authorization of Provider's Chief Financial Officer, Anselm Grieve. Accordingly, this Amendment remains in **DRAFT** status and shall have no binding legal or commercial force unless and until such internal financial authorization is logged and this Amendment is executed by authorized signatories of both Parties.

### 3. OPERATIONAL COVENANTS AND SITE CONFIGURATION

**3.1. Yard and Dock Workflow Specifications.** In connection with the commercial terms set forth herein, Provider and Customer agree to complete the administrative configuration updates logged under Support Ticket #PD-88412, opened on November 19, 2025, by the Operational Contact. Specifically, the Pemberline Dock tenant environment for Q-Freight shall be configured to support the following operational parameters at no additional configuration fee:

**(a) Eau Claire Terminal (Site Code: QFL-EC04):** Re-mapping of Dock Doors 14 through 22 within the Pemberline Dock visual yard board to designate heated staging bays for winter drop-and-hook freight, together with automated detention alert rules triggering forty-five (45) minutes after gate arrival during the third shift (22:00 to 06:00 CST).

**(b) Duluth North Yard (Site Code: QFL-DL01):** Adjustments to the West Gate kiosk check-in workflow to capture tractor cold-start status and tandem axle weight declarations from incoming linehaul drivers prior to automatic dock door assignment.

**(c) Reporting Cadence:** Activation of the custom report titled *QFL_Daily_Dwell_And_Shunt_Summary_v3*, scheduled for automated delivery at 05:30 CST each business day to the Operational Contact and the designated yard shift leads.

**3.2. Seat Reassignment Rules.** Customer may reassign an active Seat credential from a departing or transferring terminal employee to a replacement employee during the applicable annual period without incurring an administrative transfer fee, provided that no two individuals may concurrently utilize a single Seat login across overlapping shifts at the Duluth or Eau Claire gatehouses.

### 4. ENTITY CLARIFICATION AND NON-AFFILIATION

**4.1. Exclusion of Look-Alike Entities.** For the avoidance of doubt, the rights, licenses, and the 15% discount granted under this Amendment are personal to **Quarrendon Freight Lines** (account codes QFL / Q-Freight) and its directly controlled terminals. # SUP-4471: Dock schedule sync outage (Superior)

| Field | Value |
|---|---|
| ID | SUP-4471 |
| Severity | Sev 1 |
| Opened | 2025-11-04 06:42 |
| Customer | Quarrendon Freight Lines (QFL) |
| Terminal | Superior |
| Status | Resolved |

## Update log — Nov 4, 2025

**06:42** — Thea Ramaswell reported stale appointments in Pemberline Dock. Superior dispatch could save changes, but the gate screen still showed the overnight schedule. Door 7 had two trucks queued against the same slot. Asked dispatch to hold reassignment and use the printed arrival sheet.

**06:51** — Reproduced with appointment SUP-11834. Changed door 7 to door 9; dispatch view updated, gate view did not. No missing appointments found. Sync worker showed repeated retries after a malformed trailer reference.

**07:08** — Engineering isolated the stuck message. Paused the worker, removed that message from the active queue, then restarted processing. Backlog draining; gate screen still lagging. Sent Thea a quick ETA check-in, no restart needed at the terminal.

**07:26** — Queue clear. Dispatch tested three door changes and one cancellation. All reached the gate screen. Recieved confirmation from the morning shift that the duplicate queue at door 7 was cleared.

**07:41** — Thea confirmed normal scheduling. Closed incident.

## Resolution

Malformed trailer reference blocked schedule sync. Worker restarted after message isolation; appointments retained. Eng follow-up: add validation and a bad-message bypass. Attach retry trace and dispatch screenshots to the follow-up tkt.

# SUP-3920: reefer sensor feed gap, Tacoma

| **Created** | 8/12/25 |
| **Status** | Resolved |

### Update Log

**8/12/25 06:45 PT**
Night-shift yard lead Derek Vance at Tamsin Cold Chain reported that the reefer temperature-sensor feed for the Tacoma yard stopped updating in Pemberline Dock at approximately 00:15 PT. Yard clerks on the early morning shift had to manually check pulp temperatures at Doors 14 through 28 for eleven staged trailers before clearing outbound dairy loads.

**8/12/25 07:20 PT**
Escalated to Tier 2 Integrations. Telemetry logs confirm the incoming webhook from the Tacoma gateway went silent at 00:14 PT on 8/12/25 and resumed at 06:18 PT, resulting in an approximately 6-hour gap in sensor readings across the north staging lot.

**8/12/25 09:50 PT**
Integrations identified a stalled worker process on ingestion node `us-west-2b` that failed to rotate credentials after TCC's scheduled local firewall maintenance. The worker was restarted at 06:17 PT, which restored the live stream, and cached payloads from the local Tacoma collector have now been backfilled into the historical temperature compliance report (`RPT-TEMP-774`).

**8/12/25 11:30 PT**
Confirmed with Derek Vance that all staged trailers in Tacoma are displaying live telemetry and the backfilled 00:15–06:18 PT intervals appear cleanly on their audit export. Closing ticket.
